articles.title: Ayyoub Bouaddi: Man City sign Lille midfielder in £85.6m transfer
articles.summary: Ayyoub Bouaddi has completed his transfer from Lille to Man City
articles.content:
Ayyoub Bouaddi: Man City sign Lille midfielder in £85.6m transfer

Ayyoub Bouaddi has completed his transfer from Lille to Man City

Last Update:

Manchester City have signed Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for £85.6m on a five-year deal.

Bouaddi, 18, has become the Premier League club’s fifth signing of the summer transfer window days after fellow midfielder Rodri’s move to Barcelona following seven years with City.

Speaking for the first time at his new club, the World Cup star said: “I wouldn’t be here without my family, so I am really happy to have them next to me.

“This is also why I am playing football, to make my family proud.

“I think the most important thing is to have balance and my family and parents are not always [about] football.

“It’s all the values that they teach me and it’s important to keep that.

“We need to be the same person with everybody, respect everyone, be myself, be yourself and just try to enjoy life.”

Table of Contents

Ayyoub Bouaddi: Why City made transfer move

Bouaddi has long been one of the best young players in France and announced himself on the European stage by playing throughout their home win over Real Madrid in October 2024 on his Champions League debut.

With Bernardo Silva and Rodri – two of the key midfielders in City’s period of dominating the Premier League under former manager Pep Guardiola – now gone, new City head coach Enzo Maresca is rebuilding his midfield.

The Italian is overseeing a squad in transition as he attempts to prove himself a worthy successor to Guardiola, who became the club’s most successful manager of all time during the Spaniard’s 10 years in charge until his exit in May.

A ball winner at the base of midfield, Bouaddi has the potential to replace some of the abilities that made Rodri a four-time Premier League champion and Champions League winner with the club, as well as the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner and player of the tournament at the World Cup 2026.

Maresca may be planning to pair Bouaddi with 23-year-old Elliot Anderson, who arrived from Nottingham Forest for £116m in July.

The former Chelsea manager is likely to have been among numerous admirers of Bouaddi’s performances at the World Cup, starting five of Morocco’s six matches and producing an exceptional display in their opening 1-1 draw with Brazil.

Ayyoub Bouaddi style of play

Lille veteran and former Arsenal and Chelsea striker Olivier Giroud calls Bouaddi “somewhat reminiscent” of legendary midfielder N’Golo Kante.

“He’s calm, confident and remains himself,” Giroud told BBC Sport. “I was talking to some friends and they sent me some photos of Patrick Vieira and Sergio Busquets. They said he’s a mix of both.

“Technically he’s not quite at the level of Sergio Busquets yet, but he’s got the skills. He might lack the power of Patrick.

“He’ll get stronger and bigger with time but he’s already a very versatile player. He can do everything.

“The only thing he needs to work on – and he knows this because we’ve teased him a lot this year – is finishing. He needs to be more aggressive in front of goal.”

Ayyoub Bouaddi 🌟 👶 Just 18 years old… #UCL pic.twitter.com/JYYlcmKw7X

Ayyoub Bouaddi: Arsenal miss out on transfer

Reigning Premier League champions Arsenal were one of the clubs linked with Bouaddi, although their 3-0 win over City in the Community Shield on August 16 – and Anderson and Mateo Kovacic’s unconvincing performances as part of a poor City display – suggested they were less in need of players in his position.

Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City and Bayern Munich were also interested in Bouaddi, Metro reported on June 30.

Citing RMC Sport, the outlet said Lille wanted to sell for up to £89m but were willing to accept a lower fee if he was loaned back to them this season.

Ayyoub Bouaddi stats: Lille, Morocco

Lille’s trust in Bouaddi has allowed him to break several age records, including the feat of becoming the youngest player ever in a European club competition game by featuring in the Conference League three days after his 16th birthday in October 2023.

Seventeen days later, Bouaddi made his first appearance in Ligue 1 to become the youngest appearance-maker in the French top flight for 42 years.

Bouaddi signed a contract extension until 2029 in December 2025. The following month, he broke former Premier League Player of the Season Eden Hazard’s record as the youngest player to make 50 Ligue 1 appearances for Lille.

Morocco considered Bouaddi’s switch of allegiance in May 2026 a major coup following his appearances at youth level for France, with their pursuit rewarded by his World Cup performances.

Here are some of Bouaddi’s key stats in Ligue 1 2025/26.

articles.title: When is the Champions League draw? Date, time, schedule, where to watch
articles.summary: The competition is in its 72nd season
articles.content:
When is the Champions League draw? Date, time, schedule, where to watch

The competition is in its 72nd season

Last Update:

The Champions League draw for the 2026/27 edition of the competition will schedule the initial eight matches for each of the teams taking part.

Reigning French champions Paris Saint-Germain will defend the title they retained by beating Arsenal on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the 2025/26 final.

Premier League holders the Gunners and runners-up Manchester City will be joined by Manchester United, Aston Villa and Liverpool in the draw.

Here’s what you need to know about the Champions League draw, including when it takes place, when future draws are and the fixture schedule for 2026/27.

Table of Contents

When is the Champions League league phase draw?

The draw will take place on Thursday, August 27 – a day after the play-off ties come to a close to decide the last teams to qualify.

The draw ceremony will start at 17:00 BST / 12:00 ET / 09:00 PT.

How to watch the Champions League draw: TV channel, live stream

The draw will be shown live and for free on UEFA.com, as well as on UEFA’s YouTube channel.

TNT Sports will also broadcast the draw on TNT Sports 1 and the HBO Max app.

Champions League format

In a change from the group stage format conducted until 2023/24, each team now plays eight matches in the league phase, all against different opponents.

Four of those matches will be at home and four away, with the opponents determined according to four seeding pots split by rankings.

Teams will play two opponents from each of those pots – one against a team from each pot at home and one away. The results decide the overall standings in one league.

The top eight sides in the table qualify automatically for the round of 16. The teams finishing in ninth to 24th will compete in a two-legged knockout phase play-off to reach the last 16.

Teams finishing 25th or lower are out of Europe for the season.

Champions League schedule, fixtures 2026/27

The league phase starts on September 8 and runs until the end of January.

When is the Champions League knockout phase?

The knockout stage starts with the play-offs to reach the round of 16 in February.

When are the Champions League draws?

The dates for the knockout stage draws were yet to be confirmed as of August 25, 2026.

English teams in the Champions League: Why are there five clubs?

Arsenal, City, United, Villa and Liverpool.qualified as the top five teams in the Premier League.

England was awarded extra positions as a result of UEFA’s co-efficient rankings, which are based on the overall performances of nations across European competition over a season.

Villa also won last season’s Europa League, which would have earned the Villans a place in the Champions League had they not qualified through their league position.

When is the Champions League final?

The final will take place on June 5 2027 at the Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, which has been Atletico Madrid’s home since 2017.

That could be a good omen for English teams: two Premier League sides reached the final when Atleti’s home previously hosted the showpiece in 2019, Liverpool beating Tottenham 2-0.

When is the Europa League draw? Date, time, schedule, where to watch

English clubs have been in seven of the last 11 Europa League finals

Last Update:

The draw for the 2026/27 edition of the Europa League will schedule the initial eight matches as teams from across Europe bid to succeed Aston Villa as champions.

Villa beat Freiburg in the 2025/26 final, with Sevilla’s seven triumphs making the Spanish side by far the most successful team in Europa League history.

Premier League side Bournemouth are making their European debut this season after finishing sixth in the top flight, while Crystal Palace qualified by winning the Conference League.

Sunderland join them, making their second-ever appearance in Europe a season after winning promotion to the Premier League.

Table of Contents

When is the 2026 Europa League draw?

The draw will take place on Friday, August 28 – a day after the play-off ties come to a close to decide the last teams to qualify.

The draw will start at 12:00 BST / 07:00 ET / 04:00 PT.

How to watch Europa League draw: TV channel, live online stream

The draw will be shown live and for free on UEFA.com, as well as on UEFA’s YouTube channel.

TNT Sports will also broadcast the draw on TNT Sports 1 and the HBO Max app.

2026/27 Europa League format

In a change from the group stage held until 2023/24, each team now plays eight matches in the league phase, all against different opponents.

Four of those matches will be at home and four away, with the opponents determined according to four seeding pots split by rankings.

Teams will play two opponents from each of those pots – one against a team from each pot at home and one away. The results decide the overall standings in one league.

The top eight sides in the table qualify automatically for the round of 16. The teams finishing in ninth to 24th will compete in a two-legged knockout phase play-off to reach the last 16.

Teams finishing 25th or lower are out of Europe for the season.

Europa League schedule, fixtures 2026/27

The league phase starts on September 16 and runs until the end of January.

When is the Europa League knockout phase?

The knockout phase starts with the play-offs in February to reach the last 16.

When are the Europa League draws?

The dates for the knockout phase draws were yet to be confirmed as of August 25, 2026.

Which English clubs are in the Europa League 2026/27?

Under former head coach Andoni Iraola, Bournemouth finished sixth in last season’s Premier League with the help of an 18-match unbeaten league run to end an exceptional campaign.

Championship play-off winners the previous season, Sunderland won their final two matches of a superb season – part of a run of eight points from their closing four league games – to secure seventh.

Palace enjoyed a remarkable year in cup competitions, winning the FA Cup to reach the Conference League and triumphing in that competition with a 1-0 win over Spanish side Rayo Vallecano in the final.

When is the Europa League final?

The final will take place on May 26 2027 at Stadion Frankfurt.

When is the Conference League draw 2026/27? Date, time, league phase schedule, TV channel and live stream

All you need to know about this season's Conference League

Last Update:

The draw for the 2026/27 edition of the Conference League will schedule the league phase as teams from across Europe bid to succeed Crystal Palace as champions.

The Eagles beat Rayo Vallecano in the 2025/26 final to become the third Premier League club to win the competition after Chelsea in 2025 and West Ham in 2023.

Olympiacos won the 2023/2024 Conference League and Roma triumphed in the inaugural edition in 2021/22.

Here’s what you need to know about the Conference League draw, including when it takes place, when future draws are and the fixture schedule for 2024/25.

Table of Contents

When is the Conference League draw?

The draw will take place on Friday, August 28 – a day after the play-off ties come to a close to decide the last teams to qualify.

The draw ceremony will start at 12:00 BST / 07:00 ET / 04:00 PT.

How to watch Conference League draw: TV channel, online live stream

The draw will be shown live and for free on UEFA.com, as well as on UEFA’s YouTube channel.

Conference League schedule, fixtures 2026/27

The league phase starts on October 15 and ends on December 17.

When is the Conference League knockout phase?

The final will take place on June 2 2027 at the Besiktas Park home of Turkish Super Lig side Besiktas in Istanbul.

The setting could be a good omen for English sides: Aston Villa beat Freiburg there to win last season’s Europa League final, seven years after European champions Liverpool beat Europa League holders Chelsea at the same stadium to lift the Super Cup trophy.

articles.title: Marmoush set to undergo Tottenham medical ahead of £50m move from Manchester City
articles.summary: Omar Marmoush is set to join Tottenham and undergo his medical on Wednesday.
articles.content:
Marmoush set to undergo Tottenham medical ahead of £50m move from Manchester City

Omar Marmoush is set to join Tottenham and undergo his medical on Wednesday.

Last Update:

Omar Marmoush is set to undergo a medical at Tottenham after Manchester City agreed a loan deal for the forward that includes an obligation for Spurs to buy him permanently.

The deal will guarantee City £50m, with a further £10m available in add-ons, including £5m guaranteed.

Marmoush is expected to sign a four-year contract with Tottenham, with the option of a further season. No sell-on fee will be owed to his former club Eintracht Frankfurt.

The Egypt international’s move comes just days after Tottenham completed an £85m deal for his Manchester City team-mate Savio.

Spurs had been working on both deals this week as Roberto De Zerbi continues to reshape his squad ahead of the new season.

Marmoush’s departure from City is a relatively quick turnaround for a player who only joined the club in January 2025.

City paid around £59m to £63m to sign him from Frankfurt after an impressive start to the 2024-25 season in Germany, where he scored 20 goals in 26 appearances.

He made an immediate impact at the Etihad, scoring seven goals in 16 appearances during the second half of that campaign.

However, his opportunities became more limited last season.

Marmoush scored eight goals in 36 appearances across all competitions, but only eight of those appearances were starts in the Premier League. He came off the bench 13 times in the competition.

He was also included in City’s squad for the Community Shield against Arsenal on 16 August, replacing Erling Haaland in the second half of their 3-0 defeat.

The move to Tottenham would give Marmoush the opportunity to play a more prominent role under De Zerbi, while City would receive a significant fee for a player who had fallen down the pecking order.

Tottenham have already spent heavily this summer as they look to strengthen their squad.

Their permanent additions include Savio, Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke, with the club spending more than £300m on those four players.

Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi and Martin Dubravka have also arrived as free agents.

articles.title: O’Neill takes blame for Celtic’s humiliating Champions League exit
articles.summary: Martin O'Neill has taken the blame for Celtic blowing a four goal lead in the Champions League.
articles.content:
O’Neill takes blame for Celtic’s humiliating Champions League exit

Martin O'Neill has taken the blame for Celtic blowing a four goal lead in the Champions League.

Last Update:

Martin O’Neill has accepted full responsibility after Celtic suffered a remarkable Champions League collapse against LASK, throwing away a four-goal aggregate lead to crash out of qualifying.

Celtic appeared to have the tie under control after winning the first leg, but their advantage disappeared during a chaotic second half in Austria.

LASK eventually forced extra time before completing a stunning 5-4 aggregate comeback, leaving Celtic to reflect on one of the most painful European exits in recent years.

O’Neill made no attempt to shift the blame after the final whistle.

“I’m responsible for this one,” he said. “Without a doubt.”

In the context of things, one was a final which it would have been terrific to win, this was a qualifying game which we should have been able to get through,” O’Neill added.

“We know that we are a million miles from the finished article. That’s absolutely true. I think we thought that anyway.”

The result is particularly damaging given Celtic’s experience of European disappointment at the same stage last year.

O’Neill was not in charge when Brendan Rodgers’ side were eliminated by Kairat Almaty on penalties, but that defeat contributed to the eventual end of Rodgers’ second spell at the club.

O’Neill subsequently took over and helped restore some stability, guiding Celtic to another Scottish Premiership title and the Scottish Cup after a turbulent period.

The collapse in Austria now leaves him with another major rebuilding job.

UCL failure brings consequences

Celtic will have to regroup quickly, but their failure to reach the Champions League also has serious financial consequences.

Qualification would have brought a significant boost to the club’s finances and made Celtic a more attractive destination for potential new signings during the final stages of the transfer window.

O’Neill acknowledged that the club’s recruitment plans could now be affected.

“The qualification for the Champions League is major, it’s major in every aspect,” he said. “Financially, for prestige, but we have to pick ourselves up. That’s my responsibility again to do that.

“I think I said last week that if you could qualify for the Champions League there would be players wanting to come on that basis,” he said.

“That’s not going to be the case but we’ll see.”

articles.title: Carabao Cup: Leeds, Ipswich, Coventry, Hull and Brentford through
articles.summary: Forest only Premier League side to be knocked out
articles.content:
Carabao Cup: Leeds, Ipswich, Coventry, Hull and Brentford through

Forest only Premier League side to be knocked out

Last Update:

Brentford hit six while Leeds knocked out Nottingham Forest in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

Leeds beat Forest for the second time in just a few days thanks to second-half goals from Daniel James and James Justin.

The hosts made the brighter start with James Trafford forced into a sharp early stop from Ola Aina before Justin cleared Igor Jesus’ goal-bound header. However, Leeds gradually asserted control in an open first half, threatening through Sean Longstaff and James while Joe Rodon produced a crucial last-ditch challenge at the other end to deny Chris Wood.

The breakthrough arrived five minutes after the restart when Longstaff seized on Aina’s misplaced header, driving forward to slip in James, who maintained his composure to clip neatly past Matz Sels. Forest pushed hard for an instant equaliser, but Trafford was again equal to Wood’s low effort, allowing Leeds to keep their noses in front amidst heavy home pressure.

Farke’s men sealed the tie with 15 minutes remaining via a scrappy goalmouth scramble, as Justin ultimately forced the ball home over the line after Lucas Nmecha’s initial effort was blocked.

Ipswich continued their winning start by beating Leicester 3-1, with goals from Sindre Egeli and a double for Marcelino Nunez, while Callum Wilson scored his first for Brentford in a thumping 6-1 win at Birmingham.

Hull needed penalties to win at Stoke, and Victor Torp fired home a penalty as Coventry City rallied late to hold off Plymouth Argyle.

articles.title: PFA awards: Man Utd midfielder Fernandes wins player of the year
articles.summary: Arsenal may have won the title but Bruno gets the nod
articles.content:
PFA awards: Man Utd midfielder Fernandes wins player of the year

Arsenal may have won the title but Bruno gets the nod

Last Update:

Manchester United midfielder Bruno Fernandes was named PFA players’ player of the year despite Arsenal’s first Premier League title win in 22 years.

Fernandes, 31, scored nine times and registered a new record 21 assists as United finished third under Michael Carrick.

He is the first United player to win the award since Wayne Rooney in 2010.

The men’s annual award, voted for by members of the players’ union, has now been won by United players 12 times, ⁠more than any other club in England and Wales.

Fernandes is the second ​Portuguese ⁠player to win the award ‌after Cristiano Ronaldo won it twice in a row in 2007 and 2008.

“They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it’s probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment,” Fernandes said.

Manchester City full-back Nico O’Reilly was named young player of the year after his breakthrough season at the Etihad which ended with him starting for England at the World Cup.

Five Arsenal players made it into the team of the year after their title win – with Brentford striker Igor Thiago making the cut after his stunning season in front of goal.

Manchester City striker Bunny Shaw was named women’s player of the year after she scored 21 goals in 22 WSL appearances.

articles.summary: Forest ready to break club record for former Ipswich man
articles.content:
Chelsea set to make £15m profit on Delap as Forest move in

Forest ready to break club record for former Ipswich man

Last Update:

Nottingham Forest are reportedly set to pay a fee of £45m for Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

The 23-year-old moved to Stamford Bridge last summer for £30m after impressing in the Premier League for Ipswich Town.

And despite scoring just once in the league for the Blues, Forest are ready to make a move.

Manager Oliver Glasner said before the Carabao Cup game against Leeds: “He doesn’t play today, that’s all I can say. Let’s see what happens in the next few days.”

Delap lost his number nine shirt at Chelsea to Joao Pedro during the summer and was not in the squad for Xabi Alonso’s side’s win at Fulham on Monday night.

He scored 12 times for Ipswich in the top flight in 2024-25 and has 31 career goals to his name to date.

Forest have signed defender Ousmane Diomande from Sporting for £34m, alongside free agents, midfielder Xaver Schlager and keeper Steve Benda, so far this summer.

However, they have sold England midfielder Elliot Anderson to Manchester City for a club-record £116m and striker Taiwo Awoniyi to Coventry City for £9m.

articles.title: Newcastle agree £52m deal for Man City midfielder Gonzalez
articles.summary: Gonzalez will become Newcastle's seventh, and perhaps most important, signing of the summer.
articles.content:
Newcastle agree £52m deal for Man City midfielder Gonzalez

Gonzalez will become Newcastle's seventh, and perhaps most important, signing of the summer.

Last Update:

Newcastle United have agreed a deal with Manchester City to sign midfielder Nico Gonzalez, according to multiple reports.

Per David Ornstein of The Athletic, the two Premier League rivals have come to terms on a deal that will see Newcastle pay an initial £48million, plus around £4m in add-ons.

Gonzalez has reportedly said goodbye to his City team-mates and is travelling to Tyneside for a medical.

The former Barcelona and Porto midfielder is set to become Newcastle’s seventh signing of an extremely eventful summer, which has seen Eddie Howe’s celebrated tenure as manager come to an end, with talismanic captain Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon also all leaving the club.

Table of Contents

Newcastle fill key void with Gonzalez capture

Gonzalez’s arrival may be the most important of the transfer window for Newcastle, with the 24-year-old likely to become the leader of the midfield Guimaraes and Tonali vacated.

Newcastle have already signed two midfielders in 18-year-old Sean Steur and 20-year-old Aladji Bamba, while academy product Lewis Miley is a rising star who excelled in their thrilling season-opening 2-2 draw with Liverpool last Sunday.

But Gonzalez gives Newcastle a vastly more experienced defensive midfielder who can slot in immediately as their number six in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s system.

Gonzalez’s aptitude for retaining possession should make him a huge asset to Newcastle. Since the Spaniard made his Premier League debut for City in February last year, only former team-mate Rodri (87) has made more successful passes per 90 minutes in the division than Gonzalez (68), according to Opta.

After completing the deal for Gonzalez, Newcastle are expected to turn their attentions to trying to sign a forward player who can operate as a number 10 and play on the wings, with that need perhaps exacerbated by an injury to William Osula that is expected to keep the Dane out for a couple of weeks. Newcastle have been linked with a late window move for Lille’s Belgium international Matias Ferandez-Pardo.

Having allow Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Bernardo Silva to leave the club and with Gonzalez set to follow them in departing, City will now aim to complete their midfield revamp.

Can City get Enzo deal done?

City have added to their midfield with the signing of Elliot Anderson in a £116million deal from Nottingham Forest and are set to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille £81.3m plus £4.3m in add-ons.

The desired final piece of the puzzle for City in reshaping their midfield is Chelsea star Enzo Fernandez.

Chelsea had set a deadline of last Friday for City to sign the Argentina international. However, they are still said to be open to a sale if they get at least £120million and are able to sign a replacement.

The Fernandez saga will likely dominate the final days of the window as former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca aims to take him to the Etihad Stadium.

Fernandez was a 65th-minute substitute on Monday as Chelsea claimed a 3-2 win over west London rivals Fulham in their first game under Xabi Alonso.

City take on Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Friday, while Newcastle face West Brom in the EFL Cup on Wednesday before a reunion with Tonali on Saturday as they visit Tottenham.

articles.title: Carlos Baleba completes £70m move to Manchester United
articles.summary: Baleba is the latest man in as United rebuild their midfield
articles.content:
Carlos Baleba completes £70m move to Manchester United

Baleba is the latest man in as United rebuild their midfield

Last Update:

Manchester United have signed midfielder Carlos Baleba from Premier League rivals Brighton for a reported fee of £70m.

United were heavily linked with signing the 22-year-old last summer but were quoted a fee in excess of £100m.

The Cameroon international had a disappointing season after that move fell through and was named as one of the flops of the season.

But United’s poor opening-day defeat at Hull left Michael Carrick’s need for reinforcements obvious and he has signed a five-year deal.

He joins Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos as new signings in the engine room at Old Trafford this season.

Baleba said: “It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

“I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

“The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.”

Table of Contents

Carlos Baleba: Why United made transfer move

Baleba has long been regarded as one of the most explosive young midfielders in the Premier League, announcing himself on the top-flight stage with a string of commanding performances after arriving from Lille in 2023.

With Casemiro no longer at the club, Manchester United are overhauling the engine room to match the intensity demanded in their system.

A destructive ball-winner with pace at the base of midfield, Baleba has the attributes to bring defensive solidity and duel-winning presence to the middle.

The club’s recruitment team were convinced by Baleba’s rapid development on the south coast, where he seamlessly adapted to the pace of English football and emerged as a primary target for Europe’s elite – despite his poor form last season.

Can he adapt to life at United?

When will Baleba make his debut?

Baleba is available to make his Red Devils debut against newly-promoted Ipswich Town on Sunday 30 August.

articles.title: De Zerbi explains where new Tottenham signing Savio is ‘one of the best players’
articles.summary: Tottenham have spent big on a player with few goals to his name.
articles.content:
De Zerbi explains where new Tottenham signing Savio is ‘one of the best players’

Tottenham have spent big on a player with few goals to his name.

Last Update:

Roberto De Zerbi accepts new Tottenham signing Savio must score more goals, but believes his side have landed one the game’s best in one-on-one situations.

Tottenham on Monday completed the transfer for an initial £75million, spending a significant amount on a winger who has to this point struggled to consistently make a tangible impact in the Premier League.

Savio, who has reverted to that name having previously gone by Savinho, made 84 appearances for City following his move £30.8million move from French side Troyes in 2024. He was signed by the City Football Group from Atlético Mineiro in 2022.

However, Savinho scored just seven goals and registered 13 assists in his two seasons at the Etihad Stadium, and the size of the transfer fee Tottenham have paid for the services of a player with an underwhelming number of goal contributions has raised eyebrows.

But De Zerbi is confident Tottenham have signed a player with the qualities to be much more productive.

“If you analyse the last season, you need attackers to create chances to score,” De Zerbi told a press conference ahead of Tottenham’s EFL Cup tie with Charlton Athletic.

“In terms of one vs one he’s one of the best players, he can play left or right. I’ve known him for a long time, before he went to City. He’s a big player for us.

“For sure he has to achieve, so good in 1v1 and in creating scoring chances. To be complete he has to score.

“If you analyse other best wingers in the world, many of them score 10 or 15 per season. He has the qualities, maybe it’s habits, because he has to be focused on the 1v1 and to score.

“We have to increase the numbers of big chances to score and goals. To become a top team scoring more goals.”

The signing of Savio takes Tottenham’s spending for the summer window over the £300m mark.

Spurs started four new signings in their Premier League opener at Brentford last Saturday, but were comfortably beaten 3-0.

Tottenham were without centre-back and captain Micky van de Ven due to a muscle injury, while full-back Pedro Porro was unavailable because of a lack of match fitness after helping Spain win the World Cup. Mohamed Kudus also missed out having not played since January, while Dominic Solanke was only fit enough for a place on the bench.

But De Zerbi had positive injury updates on three of that quartet, while indicating James Maddison will not be involved against Charlton.

“Micky Van de Ven [will come] on the bench. Pedro Porro comes on the bench,” De Zerbi said.

“Solanke is available to start the game. Savio I don’t know if he’s ready to play or come on the bench. But great news to have Micky and Pedro Porro inside.

“Mohammed Kudus is not ready yet. Maddison suffered a small injury in the shoulder.”

articles.title: ‘Haaland leaving is inevitable’ – Former Man City star believes striker is destined to depart
articles.summary: Haaland is under contract until 2034.
articles.content:
‘Haaland leaving is inevitable’ – Former Man City star believes striker is destined to depart

Haaland is under contract until 2034.

Last Update:

Erling Haaland leaving Manchester City for another club is inevitable, according to Gareth Barry.

Haaland, the red-hot favourite to once again finish the Premier League season as top scorer, is under contract at the Etihad Stadium until 2034.

But talk of Haaland eventually making the move to Spain to join one of Barcelona or Real Madrid has refused to go away.

And Barry, who was part of the City side that famously won the Premier League on the final day under Roberto Mancini in 2012, expects the Norway star to eventually make the move away from the Etihad Stadium.

“Erling Haaland leaving Man City one day is inevitable,” Barry told GOAL.

“As much as Haaland’s association with City is really big, and that will keep him there for now, he won’t be rocking the boat like you see a lot of other players doing.”

City won the FA Cup and EFL Cup last season but, with Pep Guardiola leaving the club after a 2025-26 campaign that saw them miss out on the Premier League title for the second successive season, Barry feels a changing of the guard at the top of English football could influence Haaland’s thoughts on his future.

“I think if City’s dominance does wane a little bit and the trophies aren’t coming in, it will fuel the speculation,” Barry added.

“It is natural sometimes to want a new challenge, and I’m sure Haaland will be no different.

“It’s not just going to happen overnight. Haaland will think about his career, which is short.

“But if the trophies aren’t coming in, it will just fuel speculation. He will have offers from all over the world because he’s the best striker in the world, so it’s just natural.

“It’s one you can see happening in the future. A lot will depend on how competitive City are in Europe and the Premier League in the next year or two, I should imagine.”

articles.title: ‘I have faith in Spainish officiating’, Mourinho says after Madrid boss slams Vinicius treatment
articles.summary: Mourinho believes the Madrid star is being bullied on the pitch.
articles.content:
‘I have faith in Spainish officiating’, Mourinho says after Madrid boss slams Vinicius treatment

Mourinho believes the Madrid star is being bullied on the pitch.

Last Update:

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho insists he has faith in LaLiga officials after criticising the treatment of star forward Vinicius Junior in their opener against Espanyol.

Madrid began Mourinho’s second spell in charge with a 2-1 away victory as Carlos Espi came off the bench to score a 90th-minute winner.

Mourinho, though, was angered by the conduct of the Espanyol players towards Vinicius, who was fouled eight times in a game in which he was largely a peripheral figure.

Vinicius has frequently attracted the ire of opposing players and fans during his decorated spell with Madrid.

This February, Vinicius accused Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni of racist abuse in a confrontation between the two after the Brazilian had broken the deadlock in their Champions League tie in Lisbon. Prestianni was eventually banned for six games by UEFA for homophobic abuse, with that suspension extended globally by FIFA.

Mourinho was Benfica coach for that game, and made controversial comments in which he intimated Vinicius provoked the incident with his celebration.

But following his return to the Madrid dugout, Mourinho claimed Vinicius is being bullied on the pitch and urged him to control his emotions.

Mourinho reiterated those sentiments in his press conference ahead of Wednesday’s home game against Real Sociedad in La Liga, but expressed confidence in the officials despite his insistence Espanyol’s Alex Calatrava should have been sent off for kicking Vinicius in the back.

“The general difference between Vini and other players is obvious,” Mourinho said. “He has fallen into a spiral; opponents feel they can get away with it, so they do.

“It’s like small children—they push the boundaries as far as you let them. I don’t like the way he is treated. He was kicked in a way that constituted an assault; it should have been a sending off.

“Aside from a few things, I actually liked the officiating. I can understand the referee not seeing the kick on Vinicius that warranted a red card. I gather the fourth official chose not to intervene. And regarding VAR, I’d say they didn’t do their job very well.

“But I have faith in Spanish officiating. I always do—even in the Champions League.”

The visit of Sociedad will mark Mourinho’s first game in the home dugout since a 4-2 win over Osasuna at the end of his first spell in June, 2013.

Mourinho does not desire any special welcome on his return, but called on the fans to show the team the love that was absent for much of a turbulent 2025-26 campaign.

“I don’t want the Bernabeu to welcome me in any particular way,” he added.

“I want it to welcome the team with its passion. That love was going through a difficult phase last season.   I would like the team to feel something different from what it felt last season.”

articles.title: Tottenham sign Savinho from Man City for £75m
articles.summary: Savinho has joined Tottenham from Manchester City
articles.content:
Tottenham sign Savinho from Man City for £75m

Savinho has joined Tottenham from Manchester City

Last Update:

Tottenham have praised Savinho’s “ability, style and mentality” after signing the Brazil winger from Manchester City for an initial £75 million.

The 22-year-old spent two years at City after joining from Troyes – part of the City Football Group of clubs – for £31m but failed to hold down a regular first-team place, making seven Premier League starts under former manager Pep Guardiola last season.

“It’s taken a while,” Savinho said (via Spurs’ website), referencing Tottenham’s 12-month pursuit of him including a failed bid last summer.

“As soon as I spoke to the head coach [Roberto De Zerbi], I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level and I believe we can do that together as a team.

“It’s a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world.”

Welcome to Tottenham, Sávio 🤍 pic.twitter.com/cluPZrKRHc

Table of Contents

Savinho transfer: What Tottenham have said about deal

Spurs Sporting Director Johan Lange said Savinho had “already shown his quality at the highest level”.

“We believe his ability, style and mentality will be a great fit for the squad we are building here,” added Lange, who has overseen signings this summer including a club-record £100m outlay for playmaker Sandro Tonali from Newcastle, an £85m deal for midfielder Mateus Fernandes from West Ham and the £52m signing of defender Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton & Hove Albion.

“I know he will excite our supporters every time he gets on the ball and I’m looking forward to watching his development under Roberto’s coaching.”

De Zerbi, whose side started their campaign with a 3-0 defeat at Brentford on Saturday, said Savinho would bring “energy, imagination and quality in wide positions”.

“He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity,” observed the Italian.

“We’re very pleased to have him with us and I’m looking forward to working with him, helping him continue to grow and seeing him bring his personality to the team.”

Savinho stats: Man City

Savinho made 53 league appearances for City, scoring twice and contributing nine assists.

Of the £85m, £75m is up front with another £10m in add-ons.

The deal could represent a record sale for City, eclipsing the £82m they received from Atletico Madrid for Julian Alvarez in 2024.

When will Savinho play for Tottenham?

Tottenham are at home to second-tier Charlton Athletic in the EFL Cup second round next, followed by Premier League matches against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest.

articles.title: ‘Did you not watch the game?’ Bullish Palmer ‘hungry’ to get back to best after starring in Chelsea win at Fulham
articles.summary: Palmer scored one goal and set up another in a thrilling display
articles.content:
‘Did you not watch the game?’ Bullish Palmer ‘hungry’ to get back to best after starring in Chelsea win at Fulham

Palmer scored one goal and set up another in a thrilling display

Last Update:

Cole Palmer says he is “hungry” to get back to his best after a superb display in Chelsea’s Premier League opening win over Fulham.

Palmer scored the Blues third goal of the night in a 3-2 win at Craven Cottage, having already set up Joao Pedro’s opener in what was an outstanding display for the England international.

After a difficult 2025-26 season due to injury and a loss of form which saw him miss out on the World Cup, the 24-year-old looked to be in top form once again, starring alonside new £117million man Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro.

Asked how ready he is for the season, Palmer issued the frank response: “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready you know.

“It was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard. Obviously with the injuries I’ve had to try and prevent them and work extra hard day in, day out.

“I know the talent I’ve got so I can put in performances like that.”

Table of Contents

Palmer: I used World Cup to recharge

Palmer said he used his quieter than usual summer – due to his snub from England’s World Cup squad by Thomas Tuchel – to rest up and ensure he is back to best this season.

He added: “Normally I’m not an emotional person, the people who know me know I’m not usually bothered about things in life, but over the summer I rested, I recharged and yeah I’m ready and I’m hungry.

“It’s important – away game first is always tough but we dug in and got the win.”

‘Surreal to play with Rogers’

Palmer showed some encouraging link-up with new man Rogers, who was also on the scoresheet in West London.

It is a partnership which has been forged long before tonight, with the pair close friends from their days in the Manchester City academy.

“When you grow up you want to play or do anything with your best friends, so playing football at the best level feels surreal,” Palmer said.

Rogers debut delight

Rogers was pleased with his fast start with the Blues following his summer switch from Aston Villa and was full of praise for team-mate Palmer’s performance.

“It’s nice,” Rogers said. “You want to settling as quickly as possible, getting to go with the squad and with the fans, and to feel that affection in the first game. And obviously, to score is a really nice moment for me.

“Everyone knows how good he is. Obviously, had a difficult year with injuries and stuff last year, and you can see in his eyes in preseason in training that he’s ready this year and he’s ready to prove people wrong.

“And you saw that with that performance, that’s trying to pitch by a mile, and that’s what he does. And yeah, it’s good to own him on our side.”

articles.title: Gordon confident he can thrive as No.9 for Barcelona
articles.summary: Anthony Gordon believes he can thrive as a striker for Barcelona after a strong start at the club.
articles.content:
Gordon confident he can thrive as No.9 for Barcelona

Anthony Gordon believes he can thrive as a striker for Barcelona after a strong start at the club.

Last Update:

Anthony Gordon has already offered Barcelona another option through the middle after claiming he can play as a No. 9 following his impressive debut.

The England international came off the bench to provide two assists as Barcelona began their LaLiga title defence with a 5-0 win over Elche.

Gordon joined Barcelona from Newcastle United for a reported 70m euros on a five-year contract and was introduced in the 65th minute, replacing Lamine Yamal on the left.

The 25-year-old needed two minutes to make an impact, finding Raphinha for Barcelona’s third goal before setting up Fermin Lopez four minutes later.

Raphinha scored twice, while Lopez also found the net on two occasions and Karim Adeyemi marked his debut with a goal.

Gordon’s arrival is part of Barcelona’s efforts to add more depth to their attack, with the club also bringing in Adeyemi and Jesse Bisiwu this summer.

However, they remain interested in finding another centre-forward, with Julian Alvarez among their preferred targets.

A move for the Atletico Madrid striker is proving difficult, though, leaving Gordon’s ability to operate centrally potentially even more useful to Hansi Flick.

Asked if he could fill the No. 9 role, Gordon was clear about his willingness to do so.

“Yeah of course, I played there last year a lot. I played really well I thought,” he said.

“I have got different strengths to a typical No. 9. I can come and go and link play. I can do it. I like to play there.”

Striker a familiar role for Gordon

Although Gordon is primarily a left winger, he was regularly used through the middle during his time under Eddie Howe at Newcastle.

His versatility could therefore give Flick another option as he manages his attacking players throughout the season.

Hey Gordon, check you! 🤩Two assists on Antony Gordon's La Liga debut for Barcelona, all within six minutes of coming off the bench! 👏 pic.twitter.com/nW8uYKhaMA

Gordon also showed an unselfish side for his second assist.

He had the chance to shoot himself after breaking forward, but instead squared the ball to Lopez, leaving his team-mate with a simple finish.

The decision highlighted Gordon’s willingness to put Barcelona’s result ahead of his own goal tally.

“I think it’s the right decision,” he said.

“If Fermin had the ball and I was in his position I would want him to pass, I think it’s the correct football decision.

“We’re a team, it’s not about me scoring.”

articles.content:
Man City ‘expect Enzo Fernandez deal this week’ with Chelsea

Enzo Fernandez scored against Man City in January

Last Update:

Manchester City expect to complete a deal with Chelsea for Enzo Fernandez this week, according to a report.

Argentina midfielder Fernandez has repeatedly been linked with City, who are managed by former Blues boss Enzo Maresca.

The Italian’s new side missed a deadline of August 14 to meet Chelsea’s £120 million asking price for the 25-year-old.

Fernandez, who was exiled by Chelsea for two matches last season because of comments he made fuelling speculation that he would join Real Madrid, is “pushing” for a move his suitors could conclude well in advance of the transfer deadline on Monday night, Gianluca Di Marzio has said.

Table of Contents

Enzo Fernandez transfer: Man City ‘to sell Gonzalez’

The transfer journalist added that Chelsea are still seeking £120m for Fernandez and was one of numerous sources to report that City are on the verge of selling midfielder Nico Gonzalez to Newcastle.

Barcelona youth product Gonzalez joined City from Porto for £50 million under former Cityzens manager Pep Guardiola in February 2025 and made 51 appearances in all competitions last season, although the 24-year-old only started two Premier League matches after January 7.

Gonzalez made a brief appearance in City’s 3-0 defeat to Arsenal in the Community Shield but was an unused substitute in their league opener on Sunday, when Maresca oversaw a late comeback win at home to Bournemouth in his first top-flight match in charge.

What has Enzo Fernandez said about Maresca?

Fernandez, who joined Chelsea for a then-British record £107 million fee from Benfica in January 2023, said in March that the end of Maresca’s 18-month reign in January had “hurt” Chelsea.

Speaking after Chelsea’s Champions League exit to Paris Saint-Germain in March, Fernandez acknowledged that he did not know whether he would be at Stamford Bridge this season.

Despite sanctioning Fernandez, Chelsea’s head coach at the time, Liam Rosenior, claimed the vice-captain was “fully committed to this group and to winning here at this football club.”

When does the summer transfer window 2026 close?

The window opened on Monday June 15 and will shut on Tuesday September 1.

After that, every Premier League club can register a squad of up to 25 players, 17 of whom are allowed to be non-Home Grown Players.

A Home Grown Player has been registered with any club affiliated to the English or Welsh Football Association for three entire seasons or 36 months across their career before his 21st birthday, or the end of the season during which they turn 21.

Under-21 players do not count towards the 25-man limit.

What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day?

The deadline is 23:00 BST in the Premier League, but clubs can have an extra two hours to file the remaining documentation if they submit a deal sheet confirming that an agreement has been reached.

The deal sheet must arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes.

For international transfers, clubs also have to comply with the FIFA Transfer Matching System deadline of midnight.

articles.content:
Van Dijk backs Liverpool to finish transfer window strong

Liverpool captain Virgil Van Dijk is expecting his club to make more moves in the transfer window this week.

Last Update:

Virgil van Dijk has backed Liverpool’s recruitment team to make the right calls before the summer transfer window closes next week.

Liverpool have already added Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo and Víctor Munoz this summer, but Andoni Iraola is still looking for another attacking option.

Paris Saint-Germain forward Bradley Barcola is reportedly the club’s leading target, although any further additions will have to be completed before the deadline.

Van Dijk was asked about the situation after Liverpool fought back twice to draw 2-2 with Newcastle United at St James’ Park on Sunday.

“Everyone wants to see quality arrive regardless,” the Liverpool captain said.

“I fully trust the club and the board to make the right decisions. That’s the only thing I can say.

“Let’s see what they do.”

Table of Contents

Van Dijk calm despite lack of improvement

The Netherlands international also played down any suggestion that Liverpool’s players are putting pressure on the club to spend more.

Instead, Van Dijk believes the focus inside the dressing room should be on improving after a disappointing campaign last season.

“Regardless of what happens, we are Liverpool and we have to give everything,” he said.

“For us, we have to show a reaction from last year. We have nothing to prove to the outside world, in my opinion. It is to ourselves.”

Liverpool were forced to settle for a point on Sunday after twice falling behind, with Dominik Szoboszlai converting a late penalty to earn a draw.

Van Dijk felt there were encouraging signs in the performance but acknowledged that Iraola’s side still have plenty to work on.

“It is so early in the season that if we start panicking regardless of what could have happened today then we won’t be in a good place,” he said.

“It is down to us to make sure we improve quickly, and that is what we try to do on the training ground.

“There were some good things, but also things that we have to improve.”

"We need a squad that's able to compete on all four fronts… Let's see what the last couple of weeks of the transfer window will bring."Liverpool captain Virgil Van Dijk🔥💪 pic.twitter.com/fWWWbUdhpp

New season, new start

With the new season only beginning, Van Dijk believes there is little value in dwelling on what went wrong last term.

The defender instead wants Liverpool to concentrate on adapting to Iraola’s methods, with the squad working extensively on the training ground to meet the new manager’s demands.

“Last year it was very unacceptable, but that was last year,” Van Dijk added.

“I don’t want to talk about that – we are looking forward and looking to improve.

“Hopefully next week it will be very close to what Andoni Iraola wants us to do. Like I say, we work on it every day.

“We do long hours on the training ground and that will only benefit all of us, including our loyal and trusted supporters.”

articles.title: Rogers hails Chelsea boss Alonso and claims he could still play in Premier League
articles.summary: Morgan Rogers has some strong words of praise for head coach Xabi Alonso
articles.content:
Rogers hails Chelsea boss Alonso and claims he could still play in Premier League

Morgan Rogers has some strong words of praise for head coach Xabi Alonso

Last Update:

Morgan Rogers has revealed that Xabi Alonso’s passing in training has already left a strong impression on him, joking that Chelsea’s new manager could still hold his own in the Premier League.

Rogers joined Chelsea from Aston Villa for a British-record £117m fee in July, with Alonso’s arrival playing an important role in his decision to move to Stamford Bridge.

The England international has quickly seen what his new manager can still do with a football at his feet.

“He’s still got it now,” Rogers told ESPN Brazil. “There are certain sessions where he’ll ping a ball and you’ll be like… he could probably still play in the Prem now.

“He’s got bags of ability, bags of quality.”

Alonso’s playing career included spells at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Bayern Munich, as well as 114 appearances for Spain, and Rogers believes that experience has helped him command the respect of the Chelsea dressing room.

The 44-year-old won the Champions League twice as a player and also lifted league titles in Spain and Germany before moving into management.

“I think that helps you as a manager as well, the respect element of it,” Rogers said.

“He’s played the game, he’s played in these moments, in the big games, in the pressure situations, won what he’s won as a player.

“You have that utmost respect for him as a coach and as a manager.”

Table of Contents

Rogers ready to thrive in West London

Rogers is also encouraged by what Alonso has told him about his role in the Chelsea side.

The forward believes the new manager’s willingness to give attacking players freedom could allow him to play with the same instinctive style that brought him success at Villa.

“As an attacking player, he allows freedom and he allows rotations and allows you to play off the cuff and to be me, which is the way I want to play and the way I see the game,” Rogers added.

For Rogers, that freedom was a major factor in his decision to join Chelsea.

He believes Alonso’s approach can give him the confidence to take risks and express himself rather than being restricted by a rigid tactical system.

“Some things you can’t explain, what you’ve seen in a game or how you’ve been, but if you’ve been given that confidence from the manager to play or to try and to do those things, I think that’s where I can be at my best,” he said.

“Those were the conversations I had with him where I was really excited and really looked forward to and really saw myself being able to play in his team, which is the most important thing for me.

“I’m just excited and can’t wait to see how it unfolds and how I can be the best version of myself.”

articles.title: Maradona’s ‘Hand of God’ ball sells for £2.5m at auction
articles.summary: Diego Maradona's famous 'Hand of God' ball has been sold at auction.
articles.content:
Maradona’s ‘Hand of God’ ball sells for £2.5m at auction

Diego Maradona's famous 'Hand of God' ball has been sold at auction.

Last Update:

The ball used for Diego Maradona’s infamous “Hand of God” goal against England at the 1986 World Cup has sold for £2.5m at auction.

The Adidas Azteca ball was used throughout Argentina’s 2-1 quarter-final victory in Mexico, including the moment Maradona punched it past England goalkeeper Peter Shilton.

Maradona escaped punishment after the goal was allowed to stand, later famously describing it as being scored “a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God”.

The same match also produced one of the greatest goals in World Cup history, with Maradona running past five England players before rounding Shilton and finishing to put Argentina 2-0 ahead.

Despite its significance, the ball fell well short of its expected auction price.

Heritage Auctions had anticipated a sale of around $10m (£7.3m), but it eventually went for $3.3m (£2.5m) in the United States.

“It’s a true one-of-one item,” Heritage specialist Mike Provenzale told Reuters before the auction.

“Arguably the most significant soccer item that exists.”

The ball had been kept by Tunisian referee Ali Bin Nasser, who was in charge of the quarter-final and took it home after the final whistle.

Bin Nasser later provided documentation confirming that it was the ball used during the match, with further independent authentication also supporting its provenance.

The referee first sold the ball in 2022 for $2.37m (£1.74m). It returned to the auction market the following year but failed to attract a bid that reached the seller’s reserve.

The latest sale still places it among the most valuable pieces of football memorabilia ever auctioned, although it remains some way behind Maradona’s shirt from the same match.

That shirt sold for £7.1m in 2022.

articles.title: UEFA boss Ceferin rules out FIFA Presidency bid despite Infantino criticism
articles.summary: UEFA chief Aleksander Ceferin will not be making a bid to become the next FIFA President.
articles.content:
UEFA boss Ceferin rules out FIFA Presidency bid despite Infantino criticism

UEFA chief Aleksander Ceferin will not be making a bid to become the next FIFA President.

Last Update:

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has ruled out replacing Gianni Infantino as Fifa president but believes the Swiss could face a rival at next year’s election.

Infantino’s position has come under growing pressure following the collapse of plans to sell a stake in Fifa’s commercial operations to private investors.

Uefa was among the organisations to oppose the proposal and has since said it no longer has confidence in Infantino’s leadership.

Ceferin had been mentioned as a possible alternative, but the 57-year-old insists he has no interest in taking over the role.

“I’m not interested because of two reasons,” Ceferin said on the Rest is Politics podcast.

“One reason is that I love Uefa and I love working here, and I think that at a certain point, it’s time to also enjoy life a bit.

“The second point is that my credibility is much, much higher if I’m not interested in the position.”

Instead, Ceferin expects one of two things to happen before the Fifa Congress in March 2027.

He believes Infantino could decide to step aside if he concludes that he no longer has enough support across football, or he could remain in the race and face an opponent.

“One option is that he realises that he doesn’t have the support, and that’s not only a political support of the ones who vote, but the political support of football community, the political support of fans, the political support of the players, former players, coaches,” Ceferin said.

“And the second option that he goes to the elections in March, but in that case, I think he will have a candidate against him. I don’t know yet who.”

Infantino position remains at risk

Infantino has already seen several national associations withdraw their backing following the dispute over his proposed commercial restructuring.

The plan would have seen Fifa create a new company, Fifa Forward Enterprise, to oversee the commercial and ticketing rights for its competitions, with a 21% stake offered to a private investment group.

The proposal was eventually abandoned after widespread opposition.

Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation subsequently accused Infantino of breaking trust “through deception”, while all four British and Irish associations have withdrawn their support.

Infantino still has backing from South America’s Conmebol and the African confederation Caf, leaving the balance of power ahead of the election uncertain.

The 56-year-old has spent much of August attempting to shore up support, including meetings with Caribbean football officials in the Dominican Republic.

He was also present at the E-Sports World Cup in Paris, where he met several high-profile figures including French president Emmanuel Macron, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo.

articles.title: Salah scores first goals for Trabzonspor to give new club victory
articles.summary: The 34-year-old left Liverpool in the summer to join the Turkish club
articles.content:
Salah scores first goals for Trabzonspor to give new club victory

The 34-year-old left Liverpool in the summer to join the Turkish club

Last Update:

Mohamed Salah scored his first goals for new club Trabzonspor, netting a brace in their 2-1 win over Istanbul Basaksehir.

The former Liverpool forward, who joined the Super Lig side on a two-year deal at the start of August and made his debut last week, opened his account after eight minutes at Papara Park.

The visitors levelled in the 19th minute when Eldor Shomurodov struck from the penalty spot, but Salah restored his side’s lead just three minutes after the restart.

The 34-year-old was booked for simulation after having a penalty appeal waived away. Then, in the closing stages of the game, the Egyptian hit an audacious effort from more than 40 yards with the Basaksehir goalkeeper all at sea.

However, this time the offside flag denied Salah a hat-trick, in what looked to be an incredibly tight call.

In the end, Salah’s goal proved enough to clinch victory for Trabzonspor, who are back in Super Lig action on August 31 against Amed SK.

Salah spent the best part of a decade at Anfield before departing this summer. In that time, he endeared himself to the Reds faithful, netting more than 250 goals for the club and becoming their all-time leading Premier League goalscorer.

He captained Egypt at the 2026 World Cup, where the African nation made history be reaching the Round of 16 for the very first time, narrowly falling 3-2 to eventual finalists Argentina in what was one of the games of the tournament.

articles.title: Iraola praises Liverpool substitutes while Jaissle hails Newcastle’s ‘heart’ after dramatic stalemate
articles.summary: The Reds netted a 99th-minute equaliser in a 2-2 draw at St James' Park
articles.content:
Iraola praises Liverpool substitutes while Jaissle hails Newcastle’s ‘heart’ after dramatic stalemate

The Reds netted a 99th-minute equaliser in a 2-2 draw at St James' Park

Last Update:

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola praised the impact of players off the bench, while Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle hailed his side’s “heart” following a thrilling 2-2 Premier League stalemate at St James’ Park on Sunday.

Dominik Szoboszlai netted a 99th-minute penalty to rescue a point for the Reds after Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock had scored either side of a Cody Gakpo strike.

Elanga had given the Magpies the lead after just five minutes and held the lead going into the second half.

Gakpo levelled soon after the restart before the hosts hit back instantly through substitute Willock.

But just went it seemed as though Newcastle would take all three points, Szoboszlai swept home from 12 yards after Liverpool new boy Victor Munoz had been clipped by Lewis Hall with just seconds of the game remaining to take a share of the spoils.

Both managers were taking charge of their respective teams in a competitive fixture for the very first time,  and while Jaissle could be bouyed by his players’ showing for much of the contest, it was Iraola who left jubilant following the late salvage job.

Table of Contents

Iraola on much-needed ‘energy’

After the full-time whistle, the Spaniard singled out praise for those coming off the bench, who he said provided his team with some much-needed “energy”.

Iraola said: “I don’t think we deserved to lose. I’m sure we had more chances. In the first half, we didn’t finish anything. We had a lot of ball on the edge.

“The players coming from the bench gave us energy. The way we want to play, nobody is going to last 90 minutes. That’s why we need that energy from the bench.”

Jaissle ‘really happy’ with performance

Meanwhile, Jaissle insisted he was “really happy” with his team’s performance, despite the sense of deflation felt by the home section of St James’ Park after the game.

The Newcastle boss said: “They [the players] put their heart on the pitch, that’s not negotiable. Unfortunately we couldn’t get the three points. Our heads are a bit down but we know it’s a huge transition phase. It’s a brave project.”

Jaissle lamented the decision to award the spot-kick, calling the penalty “really soft”. The Magpies head coach also hinted at further signings this summer before the window shuts.

He added: “I hope we will do more business before the end of the window. We have some needs and we know that internally.”

articles.title: Gvardiol claims City deserved dramatic win over Bournemouth
articles.summary: Josko Gvardiol has spoken on his winner for Manchester City against Bournemouth.
articles.content:
Gvardiol claims City deserved dramatic win over Bournemouth

Josko Gvardiol has spoken on his winner for Manchester City against Bournemouth.

Last Update:

Josko Gvardiol insists Manchester City fully deserved their dramatic Premier League opening day win after his stoppage-time goal completed a 2-1 win over Bournemouth at the Etihad Stadium.

Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge as Pep Guardiola’s successor could hardly have been more eventful.

Marcus Tavernier gave the visitors a deserved lead in the 26th minute after a composed Bournemouth first half, and for long periods it appeared the Cherries were on course for a historic first Premier League win at the Etihad.

City’s response in the final ten minutes was breathless. Substitute Rayan Cherki changed the game from the moment he came on, and it was his delivery from a corner that allowed Marc Guehi to rise and head home the equaliser in the 84th minute.

The Croatian then appeared to have won it in the first minute of stoppage time when he stabbed home from close range after Cherki’s cross found him in space, only for the linesman’s flag to cut short the celebrations. Gvardiol waited.

When the VAR review confirmed the goal would stand, the Etihad erupted.

“Everyone is proud in the moment,” Gvardiol told Sky Sports. “It’s the opening game of the season and we know how important it is, especially with all the changes we’ve had in the previous weeks. We need to enjoy this, we deserve it and I’m happy with the three points.”

The Croatia international admitted the wait for the VAR decision was nerve-shredding, even if he felt confident the flag had gone up in error.

“To be fair, I was quite sure I was onside, but it’s difficult – in that moment you are just waiting to see the referee’s reaction,” he said. “I am glad in the end it’s a goal.”

The win arrives as something of a tonic after City were beaten 3-0 by Arsenal in the Community Shield at Cardiff last weekend.

Maresca will be relieved that his side’s Premier League campaign began on a more positive note, even if the manner of the win exposed areas that will need addressing.

articles.title: Messi scores but more misery for Inter Miami in MLS
articles.summary: Lionel Messi's goal could not help Inter Miami to a win over Toronto on Saturday.
articles.content:
Messi scores but more misery for Inter Miami in MLS

Lionel Messi's goal could not help Inter Miami to a win over Toronto on Saturday.

Last Update:

Lionel Messi scored again for Inter Miami but could not prevent his side from slipping to a fourth defeat in five games after Toronto claimed a 2-1 win on Saturday.

Messi reduced the deficit with eight minutes of normal time remaining, meeting a Rodrigo De Paul pass with a first-time finish to give Miami hope of rescuing a result at Nu Stadium.

Toronto had already done the damage, though, scoring twice within three second-half minutes through Josh Sargent and Derrick Etienne Jr.

The defeat continues a difficult spell for Miami, who have now gone almost a month without winning an MLS game.

They were knocked out of the Leagues Cup after two defeats and also suffered a heavy 4-1 loss at Nashville SC last weekend. A 2-2 draw with Philadelphia Union in midweek, when Messi was also on the scoresheet, briefly stopped the slide.

Messi’s latest goal was his 14th of the season, but his contribution was not enough to prevent Miami from losing further ground at the top of the Eastern Conference.

Nashville’s advantage has now grown to 10 points, while Miami remain second but will have to start looking over their shoulder with the fight for playoff positions becoming increasingly tight.

Hoyos takes responsibility for defeat

Miami head coach Guillermo Hoyos accepted responsibility for the team’s poor run but said the squad must find a way to respond.

“We’re going through a difficult spell with results that we hadn’t experienced before,” Hoyos said.

“That affects the mindset and sometimes things don’t go our way because of that.

“I’ll say the same thing I always do: when we’re losing, the responsibility is mine. Together with the people around me, we have to find solutions and get this turned around as quickly as possible.”

Hoyos replaced Javier Mascherano as head coach in April after previously working as Miami’s sporting director.

The Argentine said he had not received any indication from the club’s owners that his position was under threat despite the team’s recent form.

The loss also came shortly after Messi and defender Ian Fray were fined by MLS over separate incidents during the draw with Philadelphia, with both players found to have made contact with opponents around the head and neck area.

articles.title: De Zerbi: Tottenham ‘were not ready to fight’ in desperate Brentford defeat
articles.summary: Tottenham were comprehensively beaten in their opening fixture.
articles.content:
De Zerbi: Tottenham ‘were not ready to fight’ in desperate Brentford defeat

Tottenham were comprehensively beaten in their opening fixture.

Last Update:

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi felt a lack of readiness to fight was key to their dreadful start to the new Premier League season as they were beaten 3-0 at Brentford.

Expectations around Tottenham have risen significantly on the back of a big-spending summer, with a squad that narrowly avoided relegation last season undergoing a significant revamp.

Spurs have spent over £200million on new players so far in the transfer window, but they were comfortably second best against their London rivals as Brentford surged to an emphatic win.

Keane Lewis-Potter put the Bees ahead in the 12th minute after excellent work from Brentford’s new club-record signing Mamadou Sangare.

Vitaly Janelt punished Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky for only being able to parry Matthias Jensen’s drive as he tucked away the rebound to make it 2-0, and four minutes into the second half Michael Kayode netted the third from point-blank range in markedly similar fashion. Sangare’s fizzing effort proved too hot for Kinsky to handle, and Kayode prodded home.

Igor Thiago squandered a chance to make it 4-0 as his penalty hit the post, but that was cold comfort for Spurs and De Zerbi on a chastening evening.

Speaking to Sky Sports, De Zerbi said: “We suffered physically but we knew that before the game. We were not ready to fight the duels. We made a lot of mistakes in the timing of the pressure with Mikey Moore. We arrived too many times late and we lost too many duels to compete with Brentford.

“I am sorry for the defeat. I know we have to improve in our physical condition, in the organisation. There were many new players but it was the first game. It’s part of our journey. With a lot of new players, we knew we needed soul and style of play to become a team. Today I think there was the soul but we didn’t fight in the right way.”

“I believe in my players. Especially in the first half, we were not in the right position to make the right pressure. If you analyse the game, you can see how many duels we lost in the first half when the game went in Brentford’s direction.

“We didn’t play well. We didn’t fight in the right way. Not because we didn’t remember the last season. Because these players are good people and with value and memory. But we lost too many duels.”

“We have to analyse this game. We cannot destroy everything because we are working well. Physical condition is not the same for all players because many started the season later.

“I don’t want to make excuses but we need to keep improving. We need to find the right spirit to fight but today, it wasn’t there. I expected better for sure. I didn’t expect this result but I knew the problems we would find today.”

articles.title: Bellingham scores first goal of Mourinho’s second Real Madrid spell
articles.summary: The England star got Madrid off and running.
articles.content:
Bellingham scores first goal of Mourinho’s second Real Madrid spell

The England star got Madrid off and running.

Last Update:

Jude Bellingham scored the first goal of Jose Mourinho’s second spell as Real Madrid coach as he headed them into a 1-0 lead at Espanyol in their LaLiga opener.

Mourinho was brought back by Madrid president Florentino Perez 13 years after his departure from the club, with the Portuguese tasked with turning things around after a tumultuous and trophy-less 2025-26 season.

And it did not take long for Madrid to make a flying start to life under Mourinho, with Bellingham carrying on where he left off for England at the World Cup.

Bellingham met Arda Guler’s left-wing free-kick with a fine header, which had enough power to just beat the outstretched arm of Espanyol goalkeeper Marko Dmitrovic.

Prior to the opening game, Mourinho had said of playing Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior together: “After the tactical adjustments, it might be a little bit more difficult.

“I’m very confident that you’ll say it’s great when the three play together because they’re high-quality players, and I don’t think their positions are incompatible either.

“I’m very confident that we’re going to have a great season with them.”

But all three were included from the off against Espanyol and, having seen Bellingham and Mbappe wheel away in celebrations just 10 minutes into the second Mourinho era, Madrid fans could be forgiven for having more confidence he can make it work.

articles.title: Premier League round-up: Clarke gives promoted Ipswich winning start as Everton and Leeds prevail
articles.summary: Clarke came back to haunt his former club.
articles.content:
Premier League round-up: Clarke gives promoted Ipswich winning start as Everton and Leeds prevail

Clarke came back to haunt his former club.

Last Update:

Jack Clarke scored a 90th-minute winner as Ipswich Town celebrated their return to the Premier League campaign with a dramatic 2-1 victory over Sunderland.

An entertaining game at Portman Road looked set to end with the spoils being shared after Sunderland winger Nilson Angulo’s fine free-kick cancelled out Emersonn’s opener for Ipswich.

But there was a sting in the tail as Clarke, who left Sunderland for Ipswich in 2024, punished a poor pass from Omar Alderete by curling into the far corner to ensure Ipswich emulated fellow new boys Hull City in winning their opening game after the Tigers stunned Manchester United 2-0.

Table of Contents

Stach gives Leeds late win over Forest

Oliver Glasner made a disappointing start to life as Nottingham Forest boss as they suffered a 1-0 home defeat to Leeds United.

Anton Stach was the difference for Daniel Farke’s men, the German whipping beyond Matz Sels two minutes from the end of normal time following a rash foul by Nikola Milenkovic.

Milenkovic had earlier hit the post and Igor Jesus went close with two headers for Forest, but they could not prevent from Leeds claiming their first win at the City Ground since 1972.

Everton cruise past Palace

Glasner’s former club Crystal Palace came away with nothing from their first game under new boss Pierre Sage, as Everton eased to a 2-0 win at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The Toffees emerged victorious from their opening match of the campaign for the first time in five years thanks to goals from Kieran Dewsbury-Hall and Thierno Barry.

Dewsbury-Hall broke the deadlock three minutes before half-time as he arrowed beyond Dean Henderson.

Barry doubled the lead eight minutes into the second half, heading home from an excellent cross from Iliman Ndiaye.

Palace, who left Ismaila Sarr out of the squad amid speculation around a move to Galatasaray, lost Chadi Riad to injury on what proved a painful afternoon for the Eagles.

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes slams Man United for ‘same mistakes as last season’ after Hull humiliation
articles.summary: United made a dismal start to the new season.
articles.content:
Bruno Fernandes slams Man United for ‘same mistakes as last season’ after Hull humiliation

United made a dismal start to the new season.

Last Update:

Bruno Fernandes lamented familiar failings from Manchester United after they slumped to a humiliating 2-0 defeat at newly promoted Hull City in their Premier League opener.

Pre-season optimism around United quickly faded on Humberside as they produced a hugely disappointing display, with the Championship play-off winners belying their status as relegation favourites with a superb victory.

Semi Ajayi gave Hull a 17th-minute lead, which was doubled 21 minutes later when Nobel Mendy headed home from a free-kick.

United never threatened to produce a comeback, leaving captain Fernandes to bemoan a display that, for him, had echoes of last season’s form on the road.

Speaking to Premier League Productions, Fernandes said: “Same mistakes as we did last season every away game,” he said. “We give too much of the ball to them, in the first 20 minutes the goalkeeper had more touches on the ball, too much time.

“We need to press a little bit more, be more aggressive, and set-plays – we need to work on it, to be more aggressive and try not to concede these types of goals. We knew before the game that [set-pieces] would be a big part of their game.

“They played a full pre-season with a back four. They went against us with a back five, also to have some height, also for these moments because they could get a chance from it and defend well from our set-pieces. The most frustrating thing is that we lost the game.”

Manager Michael Carrick, meanwhile, pointed to his side’s lack of cutting edge.

“Some of it was okay, there’s bits to improve on,” Carrick said.

“It was never going to be perfect, but going behind and giving ourselves a lot to do makes it more difficult.

“It was a typical one of those games, with a newly promoted team at home. You can’t give them much, they’ve got a lot to hold on to.

“After that, we had moments and opportunities but we didn’t have the spark to put the chances away or create any more. We’re bitterly disappointed with the result, but we won’t let it knock us.”
