articles.title: 10 newcomers to watch in the 2026/27 Premier League campaign
articles.summary: Which Premier League newcomers should you keep an eye on in the new season? We take a look at the stars expected to make a splash in the top flight.
articles.content:
10 newcomers to watch in the 2026/27 Premier League campaign

Which Premier League newcomers should you keep an eye on in the new season? We take a look at the stars expected to make a splash in the top flight.

Last Update:

The Premier League’s new season brings with it the familiar promise of emerging talent. Three promoted clubs have arrived with homegrown prospects itching for their moment, while several of the established top-flight sides have academy products on the verge of breaking through.

Throw in a Kazakh teenager making history simply by signing his contract and a 17-year-old who scored against PSG without having played a competitive minute for his club, and 2026-27 has the makings of a vintage year for the next generation.

Here are ten young players worth watching closely ahead of the new campaign.

Table of Contents

Chris Rigg – Sunderland

Rigg made his first-team debut as a 15-year-old but has seen his progression carefully managed by Sunderland in a similar way to how Manchester City looked after Phil Foden.

England captain at various youth levels, Rigg sparkled sporadically as the Wearsiders gained promotion to the Premier League in the 2024-25 season and also made a positive impression in his 18 top-flight appearances last term.

Now 19 years of age, the Hebburn-born midfielder appears to have matured physically, adding muscle to a lightweight frame, and has sparkled in pre-season.

There is plenty of competition in the Sunderland midfield but Rigg should get the opportunity to shine with the club facing an increased number of games after qualifying for the Europa League.

Brian Madjo – Aston Villa

Few transfers this summer have had as complicated a journey to the first team as Brian Madjo’s, and few players have repaid the faith shown in them so quickly.

The 17-year-old striker, born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, joined Aston Villa from Metz in January for £10 million, only to find his registration blocked by FIFA for months due to regulations on the international transfer of under-18s.

Aston Villa took the case to the Court of Arbitration for Sport and won, with clearance granted on August 4. Within days, he had scored against PSG.

The Cameroonian-English forward, who drew comparisons with Romelu Lukaku on his arrival, stands 6ft 4in and combines that physical frame with close control and link-up play that belie his age.

He made his Ligue 1 debut at 16, scored 13 goals in 26 games for Metz’s under-19s at 15, and arrives with four pre-season goals already in the bank.

George Hemmings – Aston Villa

Where Madjo brings physical presence and goalscoring instinct, Hemmings offers something differnent. A technical, intelligent midfielder with the footballing IQ to operate either deep or as a box-to-box presence.

The Derby-born 19-year-old came through Nottingham Forest’s academy before joining Villa in January 2024, signing a professional contract two months later and then a new long-term deal in May 2025. He captained the under-18 side to the FA Youth Cup in May 2025, beating Manchester City 3-1 in the final, and has been used by Unai Emery as both a deep-lying and advanced midfielder in Villa’s under-21 setup.

Comfortable with both feet, Hemmings has been named on Aston Villa’s first-team bench on several occasions and the question is not whether he is ready to contribute but when Emery decides the moment is right.

Dastan Satpaev – Chelsea

Satpaev officially joined Chelsea on August 12 having signed a five-year contract with the club in January 2025 from Kairat Almaty, where he was still 16 at the time.

The Kazakh forward becomes the first player from his country ever to play in the Premier League and is, by any reasonable measure, one of the most fascinating stories of the summer window. He is not coming in blind: Satpaev has already played Champions League football for Kairat, facing Sporting CP and Real Madrid, and became Kazakhstan’s youngest-ever scorer when he netted in a World Cup qualifier against Belgium in November 2025 at 17 years and three months.

Across his 2025 Kazakh Premier League campaign he scored 14 goals and added seven assists, finishing as runner-up to the Golden Boot. The 2026 season brought seven more goals and two assists in 15 appearances before his departure.

Chelsea’s system will take adjusting to, but the technical profile, described by Kairat’s head coach as “the best player of the season” and compared to Sergio Aguero in his homeland, is built for Xabi Alonso’s possession-based style.

Kai Andrews – Coventry City

The arrival of Coventry City in the Premier League is a romantic story, and Andrews is one of the more intriguing sub-plots within it. The 19-year-old midfielder, born in Birmingham but a senior Wales international, has spent the past two years developing in the Scottish Premiership on loan.

Andrews has been at Coventry’s academy since the age of 11 and stands 6ft 1in, a right-footed, combative central midfielder with the physical profile to handle Premier League midfields. Frank Lampard sanctioned both loan exits knowing that regular senior minutes would accelerate his development faster than any alternative.

Luca Fletcher – Ipswich Town

Fletcher’s path to Portman Road is one that took him from Reading’s academy to Manchester City’s scholarship programme, and then on loan to Ipswich Town at the start of last season.

The 19-year-old striker, born in Reading and raised in Hertfordshire, repaid Ipswich’s faith emphatically, scoring six goals and adding three assists from 1,293 Premier League 2 minutes in an impressive debut loan season.

Represented by Roc Nation, Fletcher is described by the agency as “a natural number nine who can also play as a wide forward, explosive and clinical in front of goal.”

He plays with his head up, links play intelligently and has the goalscoring instinct that Gary O’Neil’s promoted side needs more than almost any other quality at this level.

Ryan McAidoo – Manchester City

McAidoo arrived at Manchester City from Chelsea’s academy and has spent the past two seasons turning heads with his performances for City’s youth sides. The 17-year-old right winger, born in June 2008, racked up 16 goals and seven assists across 42 appearances in 2024-25 including a substitute cameo in the EFL Trophy against Grimsby Town.

His 57 dribble attempts across 397 UEFA Youth League minutes last season, with a 55 per cent success rate, made him one of the most persistent ball carriers in the competition. Left-footed on the right wing, McAidoo cuts inside with pace and confidence, and his instinctive understanding of the final third already sets him apart.

Enzo Maresca’s first season will be an education for the club as much as the player, but McAidoo is one the new manager has already seen up close and been impressed by.

Shea Lacey – Manchester United

Lacey was born in Liverpool to a family of Liverpool supporters and has spent the bulk of his life proving that decisions can cut against the grain of expectation. Now 19 years old, the left-footed right winger has been at Manchester United’s academy since the age of four and a half and is entering the 2026-27 season as arguably the most explosive young attacker the club has produced in years.

Eight goals and one assist in just 458 Premier League 2 minutes last season, including a hat-trick against West Bromwich Albion’s under-21 side, two goals in 60 minutes at Fulham and a composed appearance in Manchester United’s 1-1 pre-season draw with PSG.

He has already showed exactly the kind of pressing intelligence and quick decision-making that Michael Carrick demands.

Luca Williams-Barnett – Tottenham

The Times named him in their top ten Premier League teenagers to watch this season. The comparison being made publicly is Cole Palmer. The player in question is 17 years old and has only just returned from an injury that cost him several months of last season.

Williams-Barnett, born on October 1, 2008, is an attacking midfielder who operates comfortably with both feet and was the breakout star of Tottenham’s pre-season tour, nailing a panenka in a penalty shootout win over Sydney FC and catching the eye of Roberto De Zerbi in the process.

His technical quality in tight spaces, his sense of when to carry the ball and when to release it, and his composure at youth international level. he has represented England at under-15, under-17 and under-18.

The conversation at Hotspur Way is not whether Williams-Barnett will reach the top. It is how quickly De Zerbi can integrate him.

Alfie Cresswell – Leeds United

Few young players come to the Premier League with as much context surrounding them as Alfie Cresswell, and none of it is of his own making. His father Richard was a striker at Elland Road from 2005 to 2007.

His older brother Charlie was a Leeds defender who made 14 senior appearances before a £3.8 million move to Toulouse in 2024. Alfie is now 19, captains Leeds’ under-21 side, and was an unused substitute in each of the club’s final two Premier League matches of last season.

He can operate at centre-back, across the back line and in defensive midfield, and has scored three goals and added one assist from 1,501 Premier League 2 minutes, leading the under-21s to their National League Cup triumph the season before.

Daniel Farke included him in Leeds’ pre-season tour of the United States, where he played in both the 3-2 loss to Wrexham in Florida and the 1-0 win over Sunderland in New Jersey. The debut is coming. The Cresswell name at Elland Road is not finished yet.

articles.title: Why Arsenal boss Arteta wants to sign Jarell Quansah
articles.summary: Quansah helped Liverpool win at Arsenal in the FA Cup in 2024
articles.content:
Why Arsenal boss Arteta wants to sign Jarell Quansah

Quansah helped Liverpool win at Arsenal in the FA Cup in 2024

Last Update:

Arsenal are in talks with Bayer Leverkusen to sign England defender Jarell Quansah, according to a report.

Leverkusen do not want to sell and would expect “considerably more” than the £35 million the Bundesliga club paid Liverpool for Quansah in July 2025, Sky Sports have said.

The 23-year-old made three starts for England at the World Cup 2026, although he served a two-match suspension for a straight red card against Mexico in the last 16.

Table of Contents

Jarell Quansah: Arsenal want Leverkusen deal

Quansah’s versatility is the key reason why Arsenal are interested, which England fans know about after Three Lions coach Thomas Tuchel turned to him at right-back after Reece James was injured at the finals.

While Quansah made his name as a centre-back, Arsenal are likely to use him on the right because Jurrien Timber has a groin issue and Ben White has a worrying injury record.

Arteta may have been impressed by Quansah during Arsenal’s 3-1 aggregate win over Leverkusen in last season’s Champions League last 16, playing every minute of that tie.

Liverpool are said to have a £68.4m buy-back clause for their academy graduate, who had been at Anfield since 2008 and had a loan spell at Bristol Rovers in 2023.

“Liverpool will always hold a special place in my heart,” Quansah said when he left for Leverkusen.

“It’s not just a club – it’s a family. This is goodbye for now, but I’ll always be watching – once a Red, always a Red.”

Jarell Quansah stats: Liverpool, Leverkusen

At Liverpool, Quansah made 58 appearances including his debut in August 2023, scored three goals and won the EFL Cup in 2024.

Leverkusen finished sixth last season, with only top two Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund faring better defensively in the Bundesliga.

Quansah was the 15th-most accurate passer in open play in the division, achieving 90.07%, although Arteta may hold concerns over the nine bookings he received – only five players earned more cautions.

Here are Quansah’s appearances and goals stats in all competitions last season, as well as a look at two stand-out statistics from his Bundesliga campaign.

Jarell Quansah: What Arsenal transfer target has said

“I’ve really loved it,” Quansah told the Bundesliga website of his move. “It’s been refreshing for me.

“I’ve started loving football again – being able to play week in, week out against some of the best teams in the world and showing what I’m capable of, what I can give to this team and to the fans as well.

“It’s never easy moving to a different country. Coming from the pressure of being at Liverpool, it’s not easy to come away from such a big club and try to build your own career off the back of being at one place for 17 years.”

Jarell Quansah: England debut ‘surreal’

Thomas Tuchel gave Quansah his England debut in a World Cup qualifier in Albania last November.

“It was a surreal moment I’ve been waiting for all my life,” reflected the Warrington-born player.

“I’m just so glad I could make it happen. Harry Kane even presented me with my cap. It was a super moment for me.

“[Tuchel’s] really good. He’s a breath of fresh air we needed in the England group as well, just giving us something different tactically.”

When does Arsenal’s 2026/27 Premier League season start?

Arsenal face Manchester City in the Community Shield at Wembley Stadium on August 16 at 15:00 BST (10:00 ET / 07:00 PT).

Arteta’s team host the first match of the Premier League season against promoted visitors. Here are the key details.

articles.title: Manchester City boss Maresca suggests Fernandez deal is off after refusing to meet Chelsea’s deadline
articles.summary: Manchester City's move for Enzo Fernandez seems to be off after Enzo Maresca said it was unlikely the club would meet Chelsea's deadline
articles.content:
Manchester City boss Maresca suggests Fernandez deal is off after refusing to meet Chelsea’s deadline

Manchester City's move for Enzo Fernandez seems to be off after Enzo Maresca said it was unlikely the club would meet Chelsea's deadline

Last Update:

Enzo Maresca has hinted Manchester City will not pursue a deal for Enzo Fernandez after confirming they won’t meet Chelsea’s deadline for the sale of the midfielder.

The London club said earlier in the week that any party interested in the Argentina international had to have met their terms – which includes a transfer fee of £120m – by 5pm UK time today for any deal to progress.

And with Maresca ruling out any business on Friday, it appears City will look elsewhere.

Speaking ahead of Sunday’s Community Shield against Arsenal, he said: “Not today, to be honest. I don’t think we’re going to do something today.”

Maresca worked with Fernandez last season at Stamford Bridge and was keen on bringing him to the Etihad. Asked specifically about the former Benfica man, he added: “In this moment, again, I have to give you the same answer since day one and it will always be the same; it’s a player from another club and I don’t think it’s correct to speak about other players. At the same time, I don’t think it’s correct when other clubs speak about our players. That’s why I’m not going to say nothing about players that are not with us.”

Table of Contents

Rodri back at City and given ‘big hug’ by his boss

Fernandez was being discussed due to the probability of Rodri leaving this summer.

The Spain captain, who lifted the World Cup trophy last month, reported back to the Etihad Campus this morning to have his back assessed following a minor operation.

Rodri has been the subject of two failed bids from Barcelona but it is likely the 30-year-old will secure a move to Camp Nou after expressing his desire to return to his homeland rather than extend his contract that will expire at the end of the season.

Maresca added: ”First of all, the transfer window is open; we can buy players, we can sell players, anything can happen. I just saw Rodri now in the building, I gave him a big hug, he looks good, so we’ll see what happens.”

City are likely to lose one midfielder with Tijjani Reijnders on the brink of joining Saudi Arabian club Al-Qadsiah in a £52m deal.

“It’s a bit difficult to convince players [to stay] when they are already convinced [to leave], said Maresca. “Tijjani [Reijnders’] situation, like probably James Trafford’s situation and some more players. I think when the club, the player, the manager, they all think in the same way that probably the best decision for some players is to go, you have to go.”

City in period of change, says Maresca

City are likely to be busy over the final weeks of the transfer window, especially if Rodri does depart.

They have lost some experienced players since the end of last season and Maresca is eager to add bodies to his squad.

“For sure with Bernardo [Silva], John [Stones], [Nathan] Ake, we’ll see what happens with some more, there is a change in this moment,” he said. “In the moment the transfer window closes, we need to be good enough to find as soon as possible solutions for the team. We are in a moment where players that were here many years have already left or probably can leave, and that means there is a change. We’re going to try to do our best.”

articles.title: Rangers ‘haven’t done enough’ admits McInnes after Europa League defeat
articles.summary: It's a winless start to life in charge for Derek McInnes
articles.content:
Rangers ‘haven’t done enough’ admits McInnes after Europa League defeat

It's a winless start to life in charge for Derek McInnes

Last Update:

Rangers manager Derek McInnes admitted that his side did not deserve to progress after an embarassing Europa League defeat to Jagiellonia Bialystok.

Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland levelled the tie on aggregate with an early penalty but a second half header from Nik Prelec was enough for the Polish side to go through.

Rangers will now drop into the Conference League playoffs and face FK Jablonec of the Czech Republic next week.

McInnes told Rangers TV: “I’m disappointed that we’ve exited the Europa League. The opportunity is gone and we have to say we haven’t done enough over both legs to merit getting through.

“I thought we were good value for 1-0. I thought they had a few scary moments but I just think where we are at the moment, as a team, I thought the goal would help us. We changed the shape to try to get Djeidi Gassama and Daisuke Yokota more involved.

“We stopped playing into our strikers and lost a bit of control of the game. At 1-0 the game is in the balance, we’ve still got it all to do. We had to step it up to go and get the next goal, and we never did.

“The goal was systematic of the types of goals we’ve lost throughout pre-season.”

McInnes is still waiting for his first win in charge of Rangers after joining from Hearts in the summer.

“I think it was justified to be honest,” he says. “What we served up in the second half was not good enough.”

articles.title: Reijnders set for £52m Saudi Arabia switch from Manchester City
articles.summary: Dutch midfielder only signed last summer
articles.content:
Reijnders set for £52m Saudi Arabia switch from Manchester City

Dutch midfielder only signed last summer

Last Update:

Dutch midfielder Tijjani Reijnders is on the verge of leaving Manchester City for Saudi Pro League side Al-Qadsiah after the two clubs reportedly agreed a package worth around £51.2m.

The 28-year-old midfielder has given his green light to the transfer, bringing an abrupt end to his spell at the Etihad Stadium just 14 months after joining from AC Milan for £46.5m.

Reijnders enjoyed an encouraging start to life in England, registering seven goals and eight assists across 50 appearances in his debut campaign and helping the club lift the FA Cup. However, his influence waned significantly over the second half of the season.

With City reshaping their midfield options this summer following the arrival of Elliot Anderson and apparent interest in Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández, Reijnders looks set to move on.

While interest had previously been shown by European sides including Juventus, Galatasaray, and Nottingham Forest, Al-Qadsiah moved aggressively to meet City’s valuation. The deal will also see the Premier League champions turn a modest profit on the Netherlands international.

articles.title: Leicester put up for sale for over £200m after 16 years under King Power
articles.summary: Leicester City could soon have new ownership.
articles.content:
Leicester put up for sale for over £200m after 16 years under King Power

Leicester City could soon have new ownership.

Last Update:

Leicester City are actively seeking new owners, with the club’s long-serving Thai owners, King Power looking to sell after 16 years in charge.

An investment prospectus prepared by Citigroup has been circulated to potential buyers, outlining the sale of Leicester, the club’s women’s team and Belgian sister club OH Leuven, along with major assets including the King Power Stadium and the Seagrave training ground.

The document values Leicester’s physical assets at more than £200 million, with the state-of-the-art Seagrave complex alone estimated to be worth £121m.

The brochure highlights Leicester’s remarkable achievements under King Power, including their historic Premier League triumph in 2016 and FA Cup success in 2021, describing the opportunity as the chance to acquire a club with a proven record of success and promotion.

However, there is no mention of the Foxes’ current status in League One following consecutive relegations from the Premier League and Championship.

Financial projections included in the sales material forecast turnover of more than £97m for the 2026 financial year, although previous financial losses and debts, including more than £100m in bank loans disclosed in the club’s most recent accounts, are not referenced.

Leicester have recorded losses exceeding £180m during a turbulent period that saw them bounce between the Premier League and Championship before slipping into the third tier.

King Power purchased Leicester from Milan Mandaric for £35m in 2010, overseeing the most successful spell in the club’s history.

Srivaddhanaprabha era ending

Current chairman Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha took over following the death of his father, Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha, in the helicopter crash outside the King Power Stadium in 2018.

Reports first emerged in July that the family were exploring a sale, but the circulation of the sales brochure marks the clearest indication yet that they are actively seeking new investment.

The decision comes after a difficult period both on and off the pitch. Leicester’s relegation to League One prompted protests from supporters, many of whom called for a change of ownership, while King Power’s duty-free business has also faced financial challenges in Thailand.

Despite the club’s decline, Leicester are being marketed as one of only five English clubs to have won the Premier League, FA Cup and League Cup since 2000.

The prospectus also points to the strength of the club’s academy, highlighting its track record of developing players and generating transfer income.

One recent example is Jeremy Monga, who joined Manchester City in a £10m deal earlier this summer.

articles.title: Carrick says United need to ‘keep pushing’ in the transfer market
articles.summary: United need new faces before the end of the month
articles.content:
Carrick says United need to ‘keep pushing’ in the transfer market

United need new faces before the end of the month

Last Update:

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick says the club will “keep pushing” in the transfer market to strengthen their squad before the end of the summer.

Carrick has signed Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans in midfield so far this summer to replace the departing Casemiro.

But further additions have been few and far between to leave last season’s third-placed finishers looking short of options.

Read our full Manchester United preview here.

Jadon Sancho, Rasmus Hojlund and Andre Onana have all also left Old Trafford since the end of last season and Carrick knows he still needs some numbers – though Marcus Rashford is back in the picture.

“We’re delighted with the players we’ve brought in, first and foremost,” Carrick said in an interview from United’s preseason training camp in County Kildare, Ireland.

“I think we’ve improved the group, we’ve improved the squad in different ways with balance, quality and the direction we want to go in. I think we’ve done really good business and we’ve got really some top, top, top players. So we’re delighted with that.

“We always want to improve, we want to, you know, we want more, we need more, we keep looking for how we can do that, so that never stops. We’re conscious of that and we’ve got to keep pushing.”

“There’s one or two areas where we’d like to improve and we feel that there’s the possibility to improve,” said Carrick, who added that he wouldn’t “throw out any numbers” in terms of the amount of new arrivals needed in the next 18 days.

“But again, that needs to be something that we can do that makes us better and improves the group, whether that’s quality or whether that’s a little bit of depth. That’s something we’ve got to manage. That’s pretty obvious.”

United round off their pre-season schedule against AC Milan before opening the new Premier League campaign away to newly promoted Hull City.

articles.title: Tielemans apologises to Aston Villa fans after comments on moving to bigger club
articles.summary: Youri Tielemans has apologised to Aston Villa fans after claiming he had moved to a 'bigger' club in Manchester United.
articles.content:
Tielemans apologises to Aston Villa fans after comments on moving to bigger club

Youri Tielemans has apologised to Aston Villa fans after claiming he had moved to a 'bigger' club in Manchester United.

Last Update:

Youri Tielemans has apologised to Aston Villa supporters after comments he made following his move to Manchester United prompted a backlash.

The Belgium international completed a £35m switch to Old Trafford earlier this summer after United activated the release clause in his Villa contract.

During his first media interviews as a United player, Tielemans praised Villa for helping him rediscover his best form before saying there were “clubs above Villa” and describing Manchester United as one of them.

The remarks were criticised by some Villa fans, leading the midfielder to issue a public apology on social media.

“Yesterday’s comments were never intended to disrespect Aston Villa or anyone connected with the club,” Tielemans wrote on Instagram.

“I have enormous respect for the club and I’m grateful for everything over the past three years.

“I accept that I chose the wrong words and I’m sorry for that. I’ll be more careful in future.

“I wish Aston Villa nothing but success going forward.”

Tielemans excited for big club challenge

Tielemans joined Villa from Leicester City in 2023 and went on to make 134 appearances, scoring 10 goals during his three seasons at Villa Park.

After helping Belgium reach the World Cup quarter-finals this summer, he signed a long-term contract with United that runs until 2031.

Injuries disrupted his final campaign at Villa, with calf and ankle problems limiting him to 35 appearances in all competitions – his fewest in a season since arriving in England.

Describing his move to Old Trafford after it was confirmed, Tielemans said joining United represented the fulfilment of a lifelong ambition and called it “an incredible feeling” to sign for one of football’s biggest clubs.

United conclude their pre-season schedule against AC Milan on Saturday, while Villa face Borussia Monchengladbach before both clubs begin their Premier League campaigns next weekend.

articles.title: Fungus stops play – Celta match postponed in La Liga
articles.summary: Osasuna are not happy with the short notice
articles.content:
Fungus stops play – Celta match postponed in La Liga

Osasuna are not happy with the short notice

Last Update:

Celta Vigo’s opening fixture of the La Liga season against Osasuna at Estadio de Balaídos this weekend has been postponed after a severe fungal disease left the pitch unfit for football.

The match was originally scheduled for Sunday at 20:30 BST, but following a La Liga pitch inspection on Wednesday, officials confirmed that recent weather conditions – including high heat and temperatures consistently in the mid-to-high 20s – had severely damaged the playing surface. The fixture has now been rescheduled for Thursday, 27 August at 19:30 BST.

In a statement, Celta Vigo explained: “La Liga agreed this morning, in coordination with the clubs and the RFEF, to postpone the match that was scheduled to face Celta and CA Osasuna this coming Sunday at Abanca Balaidos due to a disease that has affected the stadium’s turf, which is currently unfit for football.”

The club noted that while earlier inspections certified the field met safety standards, “The weather conditions of the past few days have had an adverse effect on the good progress of the field and led to the decision to postpone the match.”

The decision sparked severe backlash from Osasuna, who voiced “complete disagreement” with the new August date, claiming both teams had previously agreed to reschedule the game for September 24 or 25 during the international break.

Osasuna expressed their anger in an official statement: “For a competition like Spain’s La Liga to decide on a postponement on a Thursday, three days before a match, follows the pattern of last-minute scheduling changes to which we have unfortunately become accustomed due to a lack of foresight and professionalism.”

The club added: “Nor can such a decision be presented as an act ‘in coordination with the clubs’. And all this just over 48 hours before that team is scheduled to fly to Vigo. This isn’t football, it’s La Liga.”

articles.title: Taylor admits pressure of refereeing led to retirement
articles.summary: Retiring referee Anthony Taylor admits pressure led to his retirement.
articles.content:
Taylor admits pressure of refereeing led to retirement

Retiring referee Anthony Taylor admits pressure led to his retirement.

Last Update:

Anthony Taylor says the relentless pressure of elite refereeing, combined with the impact it had on his family, convinced him the time was right to bring the curtain down on his career in English football.

The 47-year-old ended a 20-year spell as one of the Premier League’s leading officials after officiating Spain’s 1-0 World Cup last-16 win over Portugal on July 6.

Taylor has since accepted a new role as director of elite refereeing with the Turkish Football Federation, bringing to an end a career that included 668 domestic matches, every major English cup final and 163 international fixtures.

Speaking to BBC Sport, Taylor admitted the scrutiny that comes with refereeing at the highest level can take a significant mental toll.

“No referee is being honest if they say criticism and pressure don’t affect them,” he said.

“You’re constantly dealing with the fear of making mistakes, opinions from supporters, managers, the media, colleagues and so many other outside influences.

“All of that can create self-doubt and chip away at your confidence if you’re not careful.”

Taylor: Demands wear you down

Although Taylor insists he always felt capable of handling those demands, he recognised the physical and mental strain had reached a natural conclusion.

“There are periods where your energy drops,” he explained. “That affects motivation and confidence, and you have to keep picking yourself up to go again.

“I always trusted my own coping mechanisms, but I felt my body and mind were telling me it was the right time for a new challenge.

“I’m fortunate that people value my experience enough to give me the opportunity to help referees in a different role.”

Family considerations also weighed heavily on his decision.

Taylor’s relatives stopped attending his matches after the abuse he received from Roma supporters following the 2023 Europa League final, when he and his family were confronted at Budapest Airport.

He admitted moments like that inevitably influenced his thinking.

“My family and friends have sacrificed a huge amount over the years,” he said. “That’s something you never lose sight of.

“It wasn’t just the scrutiny itself, it was everything that came with doing the job at the highest level.

“I wanted to finish on my own terms, and ending my refereeing career after a World Cup felt like the perfect point to do it.”

articles.title: FAI withdraws support for FIFA President Infantino
articles.summary: The Football Association of Ireland are the latest institute to withdraw their backing of Gianni Infantino.
articles.content:
FAI withdraws support for FIFA President Infantino

The Football Association of Ireland are the latest institute to withdraw their backing of Gianni Infantino.

Last Update:

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has withdrawn its backing for FIFA president Gianni Infantino, while the Irish Football Association (IFA) says it supports UEFA’s position as pressure continues to mount on world football’s governing body.

The move follows Monday’s joint statement from UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation, which accused Infantino of betraying the trust of member associations over the failed proposal to sell a stake in FIFA’s commercial operations to private investors.

The plan has since been abandoned but has sparked a growing backlash, placing Infantino’s hopes of securing a fourth term as FIFA president under serious threat.

The FAI had previously supported Infantino’s re-election but confirmed that stance has now changed following a board meeting.

In a statement, the governing body said it had informed FIFA of its decision.

“Following an FAI board meeting, the decision was taken to rescind the letter of support that the Association supplied earlier this year,” it said.

“The Association is grateful for the support FIFA provides to Irish football, but recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation.

“Given the governance issues the FAI itself has worked hard to overcome in recent years, we believe it is important to uphold the highest standards of accountability and best practice.”

Ireland follows Wales and England

The Welsh FA was the first of the Home Nations to withdraw its support for Infantino, with the English FA following shortly afterwards.

The IFA has stopped short of formally withdrawing its backing but has aligned itself with UEFA’s position.

“We take our responsibilities as a member association of both UEFA and FIFA seriously,” an IFA spokesperson said.

“We support UEFA’s current position on this matter and will continue to engage constructively on issues relating to football governance.

“We are aware of the recent developments and the wider concerns being expressed across the game. We are considering those issues carefully and will continue to work through the appropriate governance channels.”

articles.title: Doku signs new deal at Manchester City but admits: ‘I’m an unfinished product’
articles.summary: Jeremy Doku believes he has much more to give in a Manchester City shirt after signing a new deal at the Etihad
articles.content:
Doku signs new deal at Manchester City but admits: ‘I’m an unfinished product’

Jeremy Doku believes he has much more to give in a Manchester City shirt after signing a new deal at the Etihad

Last Update:

Manchester City winger Jeremy Doku says he is still an “unfinished product” after putting pen to paper on his new five-year deal at the Etihad.

Doku joined City from Rennes in 2023 and enjoyed a breakthrough season last year with eight goals and 14 assists in helping the club win an FA Cup and EFL Cup double.

The 24-year-old will be a key figure for new City boss Enzo Maresca and he believes there is still plenty of room for improvement in his game.

He told the club’s official website: “I am so happy that they trusted in me first of all and that I can continue to play for this big club.

“I remember when I arrived here from France a bit of an underdog. Nobody really knew me. I had to prove myself and being able now to sign a new contract shows that they trusted me and that they appreciate how I’ve been playing. So now it’s just a privilege.

“I think everyone wants to play in a team that wins a lot, so I think I’m at the right place if you want to win trophies, if you want to be up there, if you want to grow as a player.

“I feel like in the last couple of years I’ve learnt so much and I’m still an unfinished product.

“So that’s why I feel like this decision has been an easy one.”

Doku hoping to build on best season in a City shirt

Doku is the latest City player to sign a new deal, following on from Phil Foden, Josko Gvardiol and Abdukodir Khusanov. And he is hoping to build on last season’s success as City look to win the title for the first time since 2024.

“I feel like compared to the other two seasons, [it was] more complete [last season],” Doku reflected on his 2025/26 campaign.

“From the start to the end, obviously there is always going to be bad games, but I was more involved. I played more; I was more efficient. And yeah [there were] goals and assists. I feel like when I look back there was still a lot of games where I could have scored or had an assist.

“But compared to the other two seasons there has been growth, positively, every season better. But like I said before I feel like I’m still an unfinished project.

“When I look back, I can be happy, but I feel like I look also forward to the next seasons and to the season that is going to come now.

“I’m looking forward. I’m looking forward also appreciating what I already achieved. Appreciating that I get a chance to play for a big club like this.”

articles.title: Manchester City reject second offer from Barcelona for Rodri but know clock is ticking on Enzo deal
articles.summary: The futures of Manchester City midfielder Rodri and Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez remain uncertain with Friday potentially a pivotal day
articles.content:
Manchester City reject second offer from Barcelona for Rodri but know clock is ticking on Enzo deal

The futures of Manchester City midfielder Rodri and Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez remain uncertain with Friday potentially a pivotal day

Last Update:

Manchester City have rejected an improved offer from Barcelona for midfielder Rodri, despite needing quick funds to finance a move for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez.

Having seen their first bid of around £43million rejected by City, Barca returned this morning with a second offer of £55m plus add-ons but that has also been turned down with the Premier League club looking for closer to a fixed fee of £65m to part with the Spain captain.

Rodri himself is desperate for the deal to progress over the next 24 hours so that he does not have to report back to City on Friday to have his back assessed by club doctors following a minor operation.

City are aware of the 30-year-old’s desire to return to his homeland and are willing to facilitate a move but only if the player’s valuation is met. Rodri has less than 12 months left on his contract at the Etihad and a parting of the ways is inevitable.

Enzo Fernandez deadline complicates matters for City

City’s position is weakened slightly, however, as Barca will be aware that Enzo Maresca’s first-choice replacement for Rodri is Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez.

Chelsea yesterday announced they had set a deadline of 5pm UK time on Friday for any interested parties to agree to their £120m asking price for the Argentina midfielder.

That puts pressure on City to accept a slightly lower fee for Rodri in order to push through a deal for Fernandez.

City’s coffers may also be boosted by the potential sale of Tijjani Reijnders.

The Netherlands international is a target for Saudi Pro League side Al Qadsiah, managed by former Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers, with a club-to-club deal worth £60m almost agreed, according to reports.

It remains to be seen if Reijnders, 28, wants to move to the Middle East with Nottingham Forest also interested.

Reijnders joined City from AC Milan for £46.5m 12 months ago but has struggled to make an impact, netting five goals and adding two assists in 28 Premier League appearances.

articles.title: Inter Miami team-mates astonished by Messi’s return to action just hours after he hinted at retirement
articles.summary: Lionel Messi made a surprise return to action for Inter Miami last night but could not prevent a defeat to Club Leon
articles.content:
Inter Miami team-mates astonished by Messi’s return to action just hours after he hinted at retirement

Lionel Messi made a surprise return to action for Inter Miami last night but could not prevent a defeat to Club Leon

Last Update:

Casemiro hailed Lionel Messi’s commitment after the Inter Miami star returned to action just four days after the death of his father Jorge.

Messi was not expected back for the Leagues Cup tie with Club Leon – he had penned an emotional letter earlier Wednesday in which he questioned whether he wanted to carry on playing – but was named on the bench and came on at half-time at Nu Stadium.

His presence was not enough to stave off a 3-2 defeat as Miami crashed out of a competition they reached the final of last season but Brazilian team-mate Casemiro was quick to pay tribute to the 39-year-old.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid midfielder said: “He [Messi] sets a great example. After all, he is surely going through a very difficult time, but the commitment he has shown, not just to the players but to the club, has been incredible. I’ve never seen anything like it in my life.

“We have to say thank you, thank you for coming here, for helping us, and for helping the club.”

Casemiro’s midfield partner Yannick Bright echoed those thoughts, adding: “It’s incredible. I wasn’t expecting it and it shows how much he cares.

“When I saw that he was here, all I thought about was giving 150% for him. It’s a tough situation, so we’re trying to stay close to him and offer as much support as we can.”

Daniel Arcila scored twice for Club Leon with the Mexican club finishing with three wins from three.

Miami have little time to dwell on a rare failure and must now retrain their focus on to Saturday’s clash against Major League Soccer Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC.

Messi is likely to take on a more central role in that game in another indication that he intends to continue playing after suggesting he was considering his future following Jorge’s passing at the weekend.

Table of Contents

What did Messi write on Instagram?

Jorge, who was also Messi’s long-time agent, missed the World Cup after his condition deteriorated following a prolonged illness. He subsequently died aged 68 in his hometown of Rosario, in the early hours of Saturday morning.

Messi, 39, wrote on Instagram: “I don’t know what I’m going to do without you.

“I don’t know how to carry on. I used to just play football, and now I’m really not sure if I’ll carry on doing it for much longer.

“You were by my side from the beginning; there was so little left until the end. Why couldn’t you hold on just a little longer so we could finish it together?”

Messi reveals Dad persuaded him to go to the World Cup

Messi gave serious consideration to not playing at the World Cup but revealed Jorge had persuaded him to give it one last shot.

Messi wrote: “Dad, you kept asking me to play in one last World Cup… just days before it began was when your condition got worse.

“It was the first time you weren’t going to be there with me at tournament… but Mom kept telling me you were going to get better and that you’d be well enough to travel.

“I kept telling you we were going to reach the World Cup final so you could make the trip, this was my mission once again.

“After every match, I waited for and missed your message. That’s when I realised how serious the situation really was.

“I couldn’t stop thinking about going as far as possible, give you more time and the chance to watch one of the games.”

Messi struggled to make an impact in the final

It was an exhausting tournament for the former Barcelona and PSG star, who captained his country to extra-time wins over Cape Verde and Switzerland before a mentally draining semi-final victory over old foes England.

And Messi conceded had nothing left to give against Spain as the defending champions lost 1-0.

He added: “We reached the final, but you couldn’t be there. I wanted to win it so I could bring the trophy to you and show you another one. I couldn’t.

“My legs just couldn’t give me any more. This time I tried to push beyond what my body could handle, but I couldn’t.

“I never managed to feel physically right.

“We didn’t become champions Dad, but you have no idea how much we enjoyed every match. Once again, you were right: I had to be there and play in it… as you told me, always.”

articles.title: Liverpool: Season preview, ins and outs, one to watch and prediction under Iraola
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola's first season and new investors put Liverpool in flux
articles.content:
Liverpool: Season preview, ins and outs, one to watch and prediction under Iraola

Andoni Iraola's first season and new investors put Liverpool in flux

Last Update:

This time last year, Liverpool had earned a record-equalling 20th title in style, persuaded Premier League top scorer Mohamed Salah to sign an extended contract, made marquee signings from a position of strength and were about to complete a British-record transfer for Alexander Isak.

Within months, Arne Slot was under pressure, Salah was seething, predictions of continuing supremacy seemed laughable and a successful title defence looked as distant as a ferry trip from the Mersey to the Mediterranean.

Slot seemed set to stumble on before being abruptly sacked before the end of May, with Salah – the club’s most prolific attacking player ever in the Premier League – leaving prematurely and Andoni Iraola taking over at the start of June, leaving Bournemouth with European football for the first time following an 18-match unbeaten league run to end the season.

Reds sporting director Richard Hughes, who gave Iraola the Bournemouth job three seasons ago after the Spaniard impressed at Rayo Vallecano, appears to have taken a calculated gamble on a coach known for spotting and developing players, including Milos Kerkez, who the Cherries more than doubled their money on when Liverpool bought the wideman for £40 million in June 2025.

With Hughes out of contract at the end of the season, Iraola’s fortunes are likely to define the executive’s time at the club, although an entirely new era could be about to begin at Anfield, with the expectation that a consortium including extravagantly wealthy Amazon founder Jeff Bezos will buy a 30% stake in the club.

The age of spending limits means Liverpool’s financial might on the pitch will have more to do with whether Iraola can transform the mood to trophy-winning effect. Fans are naturally concerned about the motives of the investors, with the saga at Manchester United intensifying fears that Liverpool will accelerate away from their roots in the community towards a future ever-more obsessed with money.

Table of Contents

Summer Ins and Outs

IN

Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes – £55 million

Victor Munoz from Osasuna – £34.5m

Ronald Araujo from Barcelona – season loan

OUT

Ifeanyi Ndukwe to Austria Wien – £2.6m

What do Liverpool need before the window closes?

Right-back was a persistent issue last season, losing Conor Bradley to a long-term knee injury, as well as Jeremie Frimpong to muscle issues, leaving Joe Gomez, Calvin Ramsay, Curtis Jones and even Dominik Szoboszlai to deputise with varying degrees of conviction on any given week.

Jacquet looks a sensible addition but the France Under-21 international is coming back from injury and his versatility has only extended to central defence so far in his career, so a greater choice of players capable of operating across the backline looks urgent following Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate’s exits at the end of last season, with the experienced Araujo certain to help.

Iraola used a plethora of midfielders at Bournemouth and a new number six would undoubtedly benefit the Basque. The absence of Salah – and his public outbursts – could unite the squad and its forwards, with 23-year-old Spain international Munoz the player Liverpool have settled on so far to offer an option across the frontline and wings, having looked at alternatives including Matias Fernandez-Pardo, of Lille, and Koln’s in-demand Said El Mala.

Liverpool 2026/27: One to watch

With Rio Ngumoha no longer a hidden secret, Northern Ireland newcomer Kieran Morrison could make his breakthrough, although the 19-year-old was the only unused outfield player on the bench during the pre-season friendly against Monaco at Anfield.

Morrison broke the record for the most Under-21 goals at Liverpool last season, hitting the net 15 times and producing seven assists in 26 games in the youth teams.

Slot gave Morrison his senior debut in the EFL Cup last season and the prospect signed a new four-year contract in May. A string of suitors across Europe are reportedly interested if the academy product, who has spoken glowingly of his coaching from Iraola, is not given a chance.

2026/27 Premier League: Liverpool prediction

There are countless examples of fine managers wilting at behemoths but Iraola should be judged on his track record alone and the 44-year-old is clearly capable of restoring Liverpool to contention, especially if he can bring the best out of Florian Wirtz and Isak, who could effectively become new signings after a season to forget.

Many fans lost faith with Slot’s perceived conservatism and Iraola’s front-foot approach should avoid that. Whether he will make an instant impact is debatable, having taken 10 matches to win his first league game at Bournemouth.

Liverpool fans may also need to show patience on the evidence of Iraola’s 11-game winless run across more than two months last season.

101 Great Goals Prediction: 4th

articles.title: ‘We must feel very proud’ – Emery backs Villa youngsters after Super Cup defeat to PSG
articles.summary: Unai Emery admits he is proud of his Aston Villa players despite losing to PSG in the UEFA Super Cup.
articles.content:
‘We must feel very proud’ – Emery backs Villa youngsters after Super Cup defeat to PSG

Unai Emery admits he is proud of his Aston Villa players despite losing to PSG in the UEFA Super Cup.

Last Update:

Unai Emery insisted Aston Villa have plenty to be proud of despite a 2-1 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg.

Kvicha Kvaratskhelia gave PSG the lead 20 minutes in before Brian Madjo’s levelled from John McGinn’s deep cross before  the break, only for Desire Doue to settle it in the second half.

Speaking to TNT Sports afterwards, Emery was upbeat despite facing the reigning Champions League holders: “With a loss, you can never feel happy but how we compete, how the players respond on the field for 90 minutes – and our chances to score – we must feel really very proud of what we have done today,” he said.

Villa arguably created the better chances across the 90 minutes, with Safonov saving from Hemmings and Zaire-Emery making a crucial block to deny Joao Gomes as the Europa League holders pushed for an equaliser that never came.

Emery was particularly encouraged by what he saw from Madjo and Hemmings, both of whom started in Salzburg. “Their experiences and having days like today are very important,” he said. “They show how they are learning after their hard work. This is the way – we decided before the game how we wanted to play, we have worked the players in these positions.”

The Villa manager also confirmed that World Cup absentees Emiliano Martinez, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins will now return to training: “They are joining us after this match. They are not going to be there on Saturday but they will start training with us now.

“We wanted to give them four weeks’ holiday because the season was very demanding. We think it’s better to work with players that are fit. Overall we can feel proud of everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we are confident.”

Buendia echoes positive words

Emiliano Buendia echoed his manager’s sentiments, admitting the result stung but pointing to the quality of the opposition: “Not a good feeling. We can be proud of the game we did – we competed well, we had chances. They are top players. They get chances, they score and they won the game.”

The Argentine also spoke of the character shown in the second half after Doue’s winner: “We were there and competing very well at 1-1. At the end of the first half we had chances. Second half we were showing character.”

Despite the defeat, Buendia was keen to stress the platform Emery has built at Villa Park: “There are changes but the structure, the manager and the club want to keep. We have to keep working hard.”

articles.title: Carrick explains Rashford omission after Manchester United’s clash with Leeds
articles.summary: Michael Carrick has spoken on why Marcus Rashford did not feature for Manchester United in the club's most recent pre-season outing.
articles.content:
Carrick explains Rashford omission after Manchester United’s clash with Leeds

Michael Carrick has spoken on why Marcus Rashford did not feature for Manchester United in the club's most recent pre-season outing.

Last Update:

Marcus Rashford’s Manchester United comeback has been delayed after Michael Carrick confirmed the forward was not ready to feature against Leeds.

The England international had been tipped to make his first appearance for United since December 2024 during Saturday’s pre-season friendly in Dublin, but was left out of the matchday squad as the Reds played out a 1-1 draw at Croke Park.

Rashford only recently rejoined the group after being granted an extended break following England’s run to the World Cup semi-finals.

Carrick revealed the 28-year-old, along with Lisandro Martinez and Kobbie Mainoo, was being managed carefully ahead of the final stages of pre-season.

“Marcus, Licha and Kobbie aren’t quite ready yet,” Carrick told MUTV before kick-off. “We’re preserving them for this weekend.”

Rashford has endured an eventful 19 months away from Old Trafford.

After falling out of favour under Ruben Amorim, he spent the second half of the 2024-25 season on loan at Aston Villa before joining Barcelona on another temporary deal last season.

The Catalan club had the option to sign him permanently but instead strengthened their attack with Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi, paving the way for Rashford’s return to Manchester.

Despite speculation linking him with another move, Carrick suggested the forward remains firmly in his plans.

“He’s our player,” the United head coach told ITV. “He’s come back in great condition and gives us something different. I’ve known Marcus for a long time and we’re excited to have him back.”

United round off their pre-season schedule against AC Milan before opening the new Premier League campaign away to newly promoted Hull City.

articles.title: ‘There’s more we want to do’ says Arteta after Como win
articles.summary: Gunners boss wants more signings before the end of the month
articles.content:
‘There’s more we want to do’ says Arteta after Como win

Gunners boss wants more signings before the end of the month

Last Update:

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta says the Premier League champions are still hoping to sign more players before the start of the season.

New signing Bruno Guimaraes impressed after his £75m switch from Newcastle as the Gunners beat Serie A side Como in a friendly on Wednesday night.

Arsenal have also signed winger Christos Tzolis this summer but were not able to recruit Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid.

And Leandro Trossard and Christian Norgaard have moved on to leave Arteta looking for more.

He said: “There is more that we want to do. Every time we have an opportunity to improve the quality of the squad we need to do that.

“The will and the desire of the club is unquestionable. We want to try and do that. We cannot promise that will do it because it does not only depend on us.

“Let’s see if Bruno can start this weekend, he only had three training sessions but he looked good. He was pushing to play minutes and play in front of our fans. You sense a strong connection immediately.”

Arsenal face Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday.

The Gunners have won the Shield on 17 occasions, with this season’s match being played in Cardiff.

Arteta said: “It was a very good test against Como. It was a bit tricky today as we play a final on Sunday. To play the players and not expose them too much.

“They perform at a really high level. The scoreline should have been different, and that is where we have to improve.”

articles.title: Brilliant Brahim solo goal gives Real Madrid friendly win
articles.summary: Vinicius Jr captains Real to a comfortable enough friendly win
articles.content:
Brilliant Brahim solo goal gives Real Madrid friendly win

Vinicius Jr captains Real to a comfortable enough friendly win

Last Update:

Real Madrid continued their pre-season preparation with a 1-0 win over Deportivo.

Bernardo Silva impressed in midfield, with Brahim Diaz scoring the only goal with a wonderful solo effort before half time.

Jude Bellingham was not involved but Vinicius Jr started after his summer-long transfer links with Arsenal.

The Brazil forward signed a new six-year contract at Real last week, with the club calling the 26-year-old “one of the most important players in one of the most successful periods in our history”.

Vinicius had one effort well cleared in a scrappy first half before Diaz opened the scoring just before the interval with a brilliant solo goal.

The Morocco attacker was sent clear by a quick throw from goalkeeper Andriy Lunin, and after chesting the ball down he ran clear of the defence to fire in neatly.

Trent Alexander-Arnold was among the half-time changes for Real, playing alongside Denzel Dumfries, with the Dutchman soon going close with a powerful header.

Lunin made an excellent late double save as Jose Mourinho’s side took the win.

Madrid’s La Liga campaign starts at Espanyol on August 22 (20:30 BST). Deportivo host Elche on August 17 (20:00).

articles.title: Arsenal hand debut to Guimaraes in friendly shootout win
articles.summary: £75m signing plays 45 minutes and scores in a shootout
articles.content:
Arsenal hand debut to Guimaraes in friendly shootout win

£75m signing plays 45 minutes and scores in a shootout

Last Update:

Bruno Guimaraes got his first runout at the Emirates and scored a penalty as Arsenal’s pre-season continued with a shootout win against Italian side Como.

The £75m signing from Newcastle played the second half of a competitive enough friendly as Arsenal fans welcomed midfielders new and old.

Como achieved their best-ever finish in Serie A last season under ex-Arsenal favourite Cesc Fabregas, coming fourth to achieve Champions League qualification.

Fabregas won the FA Cup in 2005 and reached the 2006 Champions League and 2007 EFL Cup finals during his time as an Arsenal midfielder between 2003 and 2011.

Gabriel Jesus and Eberechi Eze only played 32 minutes before being replaced as Mikel Arteta looked after his squad.

And moments later Lewis-Skelly struck, side-footing home after an error at the back from Como saw a clearance charged down.

The full-back turned midfielder has been linked with a move away from the Gunners this summer but celebrated by touching the badge on his shirt and praying to the fans.

The Italian side were able to level before the break as Martin Baturina fired in after some lovely footwork.

Guimaraes was introduced at half-time, with fellow substitute Noni Madueke going close in a scrappier second period.

Kai Havertz had the ball in the net late on but it was ruled out before the sides took on a shootout after a 1-1 draw.

England defender Trevoh Chalobah, who signed from Chelsea last week, was on the bench for Como alongside the likes of former Spain forward Alvaro Morata.

Morata was off target, along with Madueke, before new signing Christos Tzolis fired in the winner.

Arsenal now take on Enzo Maresca and Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on Sunday.

articles.summary: Xavi replaces Ronald Koeman
articles.content:
BREAKING: Former Barcelona boss Xavi named new Netherlands manager

Xavi replaces Ronald Koeman

Last Update:

Former Barcelona coach and captain Xavi has been named as the new manager of the Netherlands national team.

The 46-year-old has been without a job since leaving the Nou Camp in 2024 but has been chosen to replace Ronald Koeman.

He has signed a contract until the 2030 World Cup.

“It is an honour to become the coach of the Dutch national team,” Xavi said.

“As someone who came through Barcelona’s academy, with the strong influence of figures like Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, I feel a special connection to Dutch football. You could say that, in a way, I am a son of Dutch football.”

The Dutch parted company with Koeman – another former Barca boss – after they were knocked out of the World Cup by Morocco.

Koeman was widely criticised for a tactic of containment against the African champions in a break from the team’s traditional approach.

Former Belgium and Portugal coach Roberto Martinez was linked with the job but Xavi has instead been handed his first international role.

Xavi won the World Cup with Spain in 2010 and began his coaching career at Al Saad in Qatar before taking the job with Barcelona in 2021. He led the team to the LaLiga title in 2022-23 and won the Spanish Super Cup with Barcelona in 2023.

Lukaku makes Fenerbahce move

Much-travelled striker is heading to Turkey

Last Update:

Former Chelsea, Manchester United and Everton striker Romelu Lukaku has swapped Serie ​A for the Turkish Super Lig after Fenerbahce announced the signing of the Napoli goalscorer.

Fenerbahce ⁠have reportedly paid a €6 million (£5.1 million) fee plus performance-related bonuses for the former Inter Milan striker.

The 33-year-old has played for eight clubs previously and has scored over 300 goals in all competitions.

“It’s an honour and a privilege to be joining your club, to join this ⁠club with a wonderful history,” he said in a message to the Fenerbahce fans.

The veteran striker, who won the Serie A title ⁠with Napoli in 2024-25, endured a frustrating campaign last ​season ⁠that was hampered by injuries, ‌limiting him to just seven appearances across all competitions.

However, Lukaku was still called up to the Belgium squad that ‌reached the quarter-finals at the World ‌Cup, where he scored three times.

“I want to thank the coach for the trust and the belief in me as a man, first ⁠of all, and also my qualities as a football player. I’m fit, 100% ready to go,” Lukaku added.

“For me, it’s also like a little emotional moment because after many years (I’m) going back to Turkey, where I lived as a young kid, where I discovered the professional world as ‌a toddler with my dad,” added Lukaku, whose ​father Roger played for Genclerbirligi.

“It’s going to be ‌special and a very emotional ⁠moment to be back there. I’m very proud ⁠that it is with Fenerbahce.”

Fenerbahce finished second in the league last season, ‌losing the title ​to Galatasaray by three points. ‌They begin the new campaign ​against Genclerbirligi on Saturday.

articles.summary: The Reds have work to do to challenge again says former Kop favourite
articles.content:
Liverpool lack characters, says former striker Aldridge

The Reds have work to do to challenge again says former Kop favourite

Last Update:

Liverpool ‘lack characters’ and need to work harder to compete in the Premier League this season, says former Reds favourite John Aldridge.

Liverpool won the Premier League in 2025 but were miles off the pace last season.

The Reds eventually finished fifth in the Premier League, 25 points behind champions Arsenal, with manager Arne Slot paying the price.

Andoni Iraola has come in and overseen a quiet summer so far. And with Mo Salah, Andrew Robertson and Ibrahima Konate all leaving the club Aldridge thinks the squad is light on experience.

“There were characters everywhere in the squad two or three years ago, but I think they’re lacking in that department now,” Aldridge told 101 Great Goals in conjunction with BetGoodwin.

“Players like James Milner, Jordan Henderson and Andy Robertson are exactly what you want in the dressing room and they’re hard to replace.

“The best teams I played in had characters. They made training enjoyable because you had a laugh and you looked forward to being together, but you also worked really hard. You’ve got to be serious when the time comes, but it’s still important to have fun and build team spirit.”

Aldridge won the league title and FA Cup with Liverpool in the 1980s before enjoying a prolific spell in Spain and a long spell in charge at Tranmere Rovers.

articles.summary: England defender Djed Spence is closing in on a move to Serie A giants Inter Milan after Tottenham reportedly agreed a fee of £27m for the full-back. articles.content:
Djed Spence close to Inter Milan move as clubs agree £27m fee

Last Update:

England defender Djed Spence is closing in on a move to Serie A giants Inter Milan after Tottenham reportedly agreed a fee of £27m for the full-back.

Spence, 26, was a surprise call-up to Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the World Cup but impressed in a series of cameos on either side of the defence.

His pace and energy made him a fan favourite but he has struggled for regular action at Tottenham since moving from Middlesbrough in 2022.

And now transfers expert Fabrizio Romano says Inter have agreed a price for the former Nottingham Forest man.

Should Spence move to the San Siro he will link up with England team-mate John Stones, who signed for Inter earlier this summer after leaving Manchester City.

Spence initially endured a tough start at Tottenham, making just six appearances in his debut campaign before spending time on loan at Rennes, Leeds United, and Genoa.

His Spurs career completely turned around under Ange Postecoglou. Re-integrated into the squad for the 2024/25 season, the versatile full-back impressed on either flank, making 41 appearances across all competitions and scoring his first goals for the club.

He capped off his revival by helping Spurs win the 2025 Europa League, earning a new contract and his senior England call-up.

Tottenham are well stocked at left-back after signing Andrew Robertson from Liverpool while Spain’s World Cup winner Pedro Porro is first choice on the right.

articles.title: Lionel Messi releases emotional statement following Dad’s death and hints at retirement
articles.summary: Lionel Messi says he could not have done any more to bring a second successive World Cup trophy back to Argentina
articles.content:
Lionel Messi releases emotional statement following Dad’s death and hints at retirement

Lionel Messi says he could not have done any more to bring a second successive World Cup trophy back to Argentina

Last Update:

Lionel Messi has revealed his pain at failing to deliver a second World Cup trophy for his Dad, Jorge, who passed away last week and admitted he is not sure how long he will continue playing.

Messi’s Argentina reached the final in New Jersey last month but were unable to hold off Spain, who won 1-0 thanks to Ferran Torres’ extra-time strike.

Jorge, who was also Messi’s long-time agent, missed the tournament after his condition deteriorated following a prolonged illness. He subsequently died aged 68 in his hometown of Rosario, in the early hours of Saturday morning.

Messi, 39, wrote on Instagram: “I don’t know what I’m going to do without you.

“I don’t know how to carry on. I used to just play football, and now I’m really not sure if I’ll carry on doing it for much longer.

“You were by my side from the beginning; there was so little left until the end. Why couldn’t you hold on just a little longer so we could finish it together?”

Table of Contents

Messi reveals Dad persuaded him to go to the World Cup

Messi gave serious consideration to not playing at the World Cup but revealed Jorge had persuaded him to give it one last shot.

Messi wrote: “Dad, you kept asking me to play in one last World Cup… just days before it began was when your condition got worse.

“It was the first time you weren’t going to be there with me at tournament… but Mom kept telling me you were going to get better and that you’d be well enough to travel.

“I kept telling you we were going to reach the World Cup final so you could make the trip, this was my mission once again.

“After every match, I waited for and missed your message. That’s when I realised how serious the situation really was.

“I couldn’t stop thinking about going as far as possible, give you more time and the chance to watch one of the games.”

Messi struggled to make an impact in the final

It was an exhausting tournament for the former Barcelona and PSG star, who captained his country to extra-time wins over Cape Verde and Switzerland before a mentally draining semi-final victory over old foes England.

And Messi conceded had nothing left to give against Spain.

He added: “We reached the final, but you couldn’t be there. I wanted to win it so I could bring the trophy to you and show you another one. I couldn’t.

“My legs just couldn’t give me any more. This time I tried to push beyond what my body could handle, but I couldn’t.

“I never managed to feel physically right.

“We didn’t become champions Dad, but you have no idea how much we enjoyed every match. Once again, you were right: I had to be there and play in it… as you told me, always.”

Messi legacy lives on

Jorge was survived by his wife, Celia, and their four children: Lionel, Rodrigo, Matias and María Sol.

Messi’s boyhood club, Newell’s Old Boys, led the tributes.

“Newell’s Old Boys mourn with profound pain and sorrow the passing of Jorge Messi,” the club said.

“He was a renowned Newell’s supporter, businessman and the father of the captain of the Argentina national team, Lionel Messi.

“Jorge was the support and the person who, together with his wife, Celia, strengthened the career of the greatest player of all time with vision, rigour and affection.

“His constant support and behind-the-scenes leadership were fundamental in supporting every step of Lionel’s journey.”

Jorge worked in a steel factory in Rosario before moving to Europe when Messi joined Barcelona’s academy in 2000.

He went on to oversee his son’s career as his agent, guiding moves from Barcelona to PSG and later Inter Miami, while helping manage one of the most successful careers in football history.

Messi is currently taking time out from football and will only be considered for Miami duty when he feels ready to return to Florida. He has two years left on the three-year deal he signed in 2025.

articles.title: Rodri hopes Barcelona can agree fee with City to avoid return to Manchester
articles.summary: Rodri is hoping his move from Manchester City to Barcelona can be sorted by Friday, and save him a trip to England
articles.content:
Rodri hopes Barcelona can agree fee with City to avoid return to Manchester

Rodri is hoping his move from Manchester City to Barcelona can be sorted by Friday, and save him a trip to England

Last Update:

Rodri is desperately hoping Barcelona can agree a fee with Manchester City by Friday so that he does not have to return to England.

The 30-year-old has his heart set on a move to Camp Nou after opting to join the defending La Liga champions and snub interest from their arch-rivals Real Madrid.

Rodri is believed to be house hunting in Catalonia but is expected back at the Etihad Training Campus on Friday to enable City medics to assess his fitness following a minor back operation.

Spain’s World Cup-winning captain would rather remain in Barcelona and avoid a trip back to Manchester but that depends on whether the two clubs can agree a fee.

Barca have offered around £43million for the former Atletico Madrid midfielder but City are holding out for nearer £60m even though he has now entered the final year of his contract.

Reports in Spain suggest the two clubs will likely settle for a fee somewhere in the middle although City are acutely aware of Barca’s need to get the deal done after president Joan Laporta publicly announced the club had agreed personal terms with the player.

Rodri a priority for Barcelona as Real Madrid strengthen

Rodri’s signing is seen as key for the Catalans if they want to retain the title they have won in each of the past two seasons, and especially with Real Madrid likely to be revitalised following the return of Jose Mourinho as coach and a summer of heavy recruitment at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Madrid have brought in the likes of Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konate, Marc Cucurella and club-record signing Yan Diomande as well as renewing winger Vinicius Jr on a new, long-term contract.

Barca have been quiet in comparison with Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi their only major acquisitions.

They are also waiting on news of midfielder Frenkie De Jong’s knee injury with reports suggesting the club are getting increasingly frustrated with the Netherlands international.

De Jong returned from the World Cup with a partial tear of a meniscus cruciate ligament but wants it to heal with rest and rehabilitation. Barca, though, want him to undergo surgery as they feel that would lead to a quicker recovery period.

That has led to an uncomfortable stand-off with De Jong’s method showing little sign of progress.

articles.title: Manchester City sign goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli for a second time
articles.summary: Manchester City have bolstered their goalkeeping ranks by signing experienced Argentine Geronimo Rulli
articles.content:
Manchester City sign goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli for a second time

Manchester City have bolstered their goalkeeping ranks by signing experienced Argentine Geronimo Rulli

Last Update:

Manchester City have signed goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille to act as back-up to established number one Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Rulli is reported to have cost City £1.7million and will fill the same role occupied by James Trafford last season. Trafford last week joined Leeds in a £45m deal.

The 34-year-old has signed for City before, in the summer of 2016, but left midway through the following season without making an appearance.

“This is an amazing opportunity for me and one I had to grasp,” Rulli told the club’s official website. “When the chance to join Manchester City comes along you have to go for it.

“Everyone knows what an impressive club this is. City’s success over a long time has been impressive. Everyone I have spoken to about City said I had to join them because they are a club with incredibly high standards.

“Every professional wants to be in a high-performance environment and I can’t wait to get started because I know I will improve and learn, which is always my main priority.

“My job now is to train hard, get to know the players and staff and do everything I can to reach my best level.”

Table of Contents

City chief Viana delighted to bring in Rulli

Rulli has had spells with Real Sociedad, Montpellier, Villarreal, Ajax and Marseille and City’s director of football Hugo Viana was pleased to have brought in the experienced Argentina international, who was one of the aggressors in the fracas that marred the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup final against Spain.

“It’s a pleasure to welcome Gerónimo back to the club,” Viana said. “The experience he brings is obvious – he has played at the very highest level for many years.

“I have been really impressed by him during our conversations, a strong desire to join us. It’s clear we are getting a brilliant professional, as well as a top ‘keeper.

“Everyone at City is looking forward to welcoming him back to the club. The qualities he will bring are ones we need, and together with Gigio and Marcus [Bettinelli] make a great team. Our goalkeeper coaches are really happy with the group.”

City still with work to do before window closes

City are likely to be active over the closing weeks of the transfer window with both incomings and departures expected.

The headline outgoing is likely to be Spain captain Rodri, over whom City are in talks with Barcelona, while Savinho and Tijjani Reijnders could also leave.

City are believed to be close to signing Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.
